clubs.name: Academic Success Programs
clubs.description: Academic Success Programs (ASP) provides a holistic approach to student development through a network of comprehensive programs and services. Through an array of retention-based opportunities, educational and personal advising, transitional programming, tutoring, skill-building seminars and mentoring programs, ASP participants receive supportive services throughout their college experience. ASP seeks to foster collaborative partnerships with University departments, external organizations and alumni.

clubs.name: Alexander Hamilton Society
clubs.description: The Columbia University chapter of The Alexander Hamilton Society dedicates itself to the promotion of constructive debate on basic principles and contemporary issues in foreign, economic and national security policies.

clubs.name: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
clubs.description: Columbia University's student branch of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics focuses on the design and construction of model aircrafts to compete in the highly respected aeronautics event, AIAA Design-Build-Fly.

clubs.name: Application Development Initiative
clubs.description: Application Development Initiative is a student group at Columbia University that aims to foster a community of students interested in technology.

clubs.name: Biomedical Engineering Society
clubs.description: Columbia Biomedical Engineering Society is dedicated to building, supporting and expanding the biomedical engineering community at Columbia University.

clubs.name: BlueShift
clubs.description: BlueShift is a space for space enthusiasts to learn about astronomy, current research in astrophysics, and how to successfully traverse through college.

clubs.name: Chandler Society for Undergraduate Chemistry
clubs.description: The Chandler Society for Undergraduate Chemistry is a club run by undergraduates for the purpose of promoting enjoyment and knowledge of science, particularly chemistry, both on and off campus.

clubs.name: Columbia College Committee on Instruction
clubs.description: The Committee on Instruction (COI) is responsible for approving proposals for new majors and other academic programs, new courses, and policy changes. The COI also provides leadership on a range of academic matters, consulting with a broad range of faculty, students, and administrators where relevant. The COI is a joint Columbia College and School of General Studies committee.

clubs.name: Columbia College Committee on the Core
clubs.description: The Committee on the Core (COC) is responsible for all matters regarding the Core Curriculum.

clubs.name: Columbia Debate Society
clubs.description: From competing at parliamentary debate tournaments around the country to participating in paid public debates to doing volunteer work, Columbia Debate Society represents the best of what Columbia University has to offer.

clubs.name: Columbia Group of Language-Oriented Thinkers
clubs.description: Columbia Group of Language-Oriented Thinkers (GLOT) was founded to give Columbia students a place to express our love for learning languages and linguistics. Although there are many opportunities for Columbia to learn languages through language classes, our community would benefit from having a club that sought to connect native speakers with those interested in particular languages; providing a space for language learners in general to meet one another; and providing support to students interested in pursuing linguistics, which is a distinct field of study from foreign languages/literatures, and a relatively new (yet rapidly growing) program of study at Columbia.

clubs.name: Columbia International Relations Council and Association (CIRCA)
clubs.description: The Columbia International Relations Council and Association is an international relations organization operated and coordinated by Columbia University undergraduates. Founded in 1989, it is one of the University's largest student-run organization with over 400 active members.

clubs.name: Columbia Mandarin Debate Society (CMDA)
clubs.description: Columbia Mandarin Debate Society (CMDA) is an undergraduate academic organization at Columbia University aimed to helping undergraduate students enhance their pursuit of Chinese/Mandarin academic practice through events including, but not limited to, debate tournaments, professional workshops, lunch chats, mentorship tutoring, and career panels. By learning and practicing with professionals in Mandarin debate fields, CMDA members gain support and guidance from debate masters to express themselves and advocate for their opinions openly and bravely.

clubs.name: Columbia Society of Physics Students
clubs.description: To provide a space for physics enthusiasts to converge, learn, gain opportunities, and to spread the enjoyment of physics.

clubs.name: Columbia Space Initiative
clubs.description: The Columbia Space Initiative is a student space technology and outreach club founded in 2015. It serves as an umbrella organization for mission teams involved in everything from nanosatellite mechanical design to hosting space policy forums.

clubs.name: Columbia University Systems Biology Initiative
clubs.description: At the intersection of medicine, biological research, engineering, and computer science, systems biology is a rapidly growing field that provides science with the ability to manipulate life processes more effectively than ever. We explore complex biological interactions through the engineering of new biological mechanisms that currently do not exist, the redesigning of biological mechanisms for a synthetic purpose, and the computational modeling of complex biological systems.

clubs.name: CU Environmental Biology Society
clubs.description: The Columbia University Environmental Biology Society is a club for nature lovers in the Columbia community. It hosts environmental-themed events on campus and leads excursions for zoos, museums and hiking.

clubs.name: CUSP Alliance
clubs.description: The purpose of the CUSP Alliance is to place the Columbia Undergraduate Scholars Program in the hands of the Scholars by recognizing and formalizing a core of proactive Scholar leaders who desire to play an integral role in developing the Program. The CUSP Alliance offers the Scholars creative and constructive opportunities to serve as ambassadors between the CUSP administration, the Scholar population, and the greater Columbia, New York City, and global communities. They gain experience organizing and facilitating long-term community and civic programming that serves not only as an opportunity to foster a sense of community within CUSP but as one of many examples of the powerful results possible through application of CUSP ideologies.

clubs.name: Kraft Global Fellows Program
clubs.description: The Office of the University Chaplain’s Kraft Global Fellows Program is an initiative of the Kraft Family Fund for Intercultural and Interfaith Awareness. At designated academic breaks, the Kraft Global Fellows Program will support up to five students to travel to one of the Columbia Global Centers (CGC) as a team to conduct research for a particular set of questions or inquiries.

clubs.name: Latinx Professional Education Network (LPEN)
clubs.description: The Latinx Professional Education Network is the nation’s leading Hispanic scholarship organization providing the Hispanic community with more college scholarships and outreach support than any other organizations in the country.

clubs.name: Mock Trial
clubs.description: Mock Trial is a competitive activity in which teams simulate a real trial. The activity requires students to critically analyze the law, interpret legal facts, speak compellingly and think well on their feet.

clubs.name: Neuroscience Society
clubs.description: Columbia Neuroscience Society aims to create a community among students with an interest in neuroscience, regardless of major.

clubs.name: Philolexian Society
clubs.description: Philo is Columbia University's oldest and classiest student organization. Formally established in 1802 by associates of Alexander Hamilton, but with roots reaching as far back as 1766, the Society promotes literary awareness and the art of rhetoric among its members, who have ranged from Allen Ginsberg to Jacques Barzun.

clubs.name: Political Science Students Association
clubs.description: As the only non-partisan political group on campus, Political Science Students Association shows prospective and current Political Science majors the benefits of the Political Science Department. In addition to connecting students with Columbia's department and faculty, the organization plans educational events pertaining to politics, government, current events and international relations.

clubs.name: Quiz Bowl
clubs.description: The Quiz Bowl club competes in academic trivia competitions hosted by schools throughout the New England and Mid-Atlantic regions, and also organizes intramural contests on campus.

clubs.name: Research Cluster on Science and Subjectivity
Robotics
clubs.description: Robotics is a community of students passionate about exploring the exciting world of robotics and autonomous systems. Members of the group work together to build robotic systems while developing meaningful technical and teamwork skills.

clubs.name: Spectra
clubs.description: Spectra, formerly the Columbia Society for Women in Physics, is a group comprised of undergraduate students, graduate students, and postdoctorates from Columbia University with the purpose of connecting and promoting women and other underrepresented groups in the field of physics.

clubs.name: Student Union for Sustainable Development
clubs.description: Student Union for Sustainable Development is a student organization at Columbia University working to connect students with opportunities on campus at the Earth Institute and beyond.

clubs.name: Symposium
clubs.description: Symposium is a student-led club and non-profit organization at Columbia University that is dedicated to promoting cross-cultural dialogues through humanities-based seminars.

clubs.name: Women and Gender Diverse in Computer Science
clubs.description: Women and Gender Diverse in Computer Science encourages, guides and provides outreach to women and gender diverse undergraduates, graduate students and postdoctoral students within computer science, as well as faculty and staff.

clubs.name: 3v3 Basketball Tournament
clubs.description:
Welcome to Columbia University's Intramural Sports!

Take this opportunity to embrace sports, hang out with friends and relieve stress.

Intramural sports — basketball 3v3.

clubs.name: 5v5 Basketball League
clubs.description:
Welcome to Columbia University's Intramural Sports!

Take this opportunity to embrace sports, hang out with friends and relieve stress.

Intramural sports — basketball 5v5.

clubs.name: 7v7 Outdoor Soccer League
clubs.description:
Welcome to Columbia University's Intramural Sports!

Take this opportunity to embrace sports, hang out with friends and relieve stress.

Intramural sports — soccer 7v7.

clubs.name: Aikido
clubs.description: Aikido is a modern Japanese martial art that teaches coordination of mind and body to develop calmness in action and the strongest human​ condition. It is a highly effective system of self-defense that does not depend on muscular strength but instead focuses on blending with an attack to redirect its energy back upon an opponent. Aikido techniques can be effective without harming the attacker, making practice comfortable and ethical self-defense an ideal. The Aikido club is a great place to lean about your inner-self and gain confidence in your abilities with like-minded aikido-ka looking to have a good time.

clubs.name: Archery (Club)
clubs.description: The Archery Club seeks to provide the affiliates of Columbia University with a safe and friendly environment to learn the sport while fostering a sense of community. As the club is non-competitive and unaffiliated with the team, we accept members of all skill levels, and strongly encourage those interested to join regardless of experience. We provide equipment for those members without their own archery gear and offer professional coaching for archers in safety, shooting form, and equipment maintenance. Additionally the club holds open practices where all members are welcome to come in and practice. To provide our archers with experience with archery competitions, the club aims attends several tournaments in the spring semester in the collegiate and guest divisions. Please visit our website for information on upcoming practices, competitions, etc. and join our mailing list to stay update.

clubs.name: Badminton
clubs.description: The Columbia University Badminton Club is only on-campus badminton organization that caters to Columbia University students, faculty, staff and alumni who have a Dodge Fitness Center membership. The club is a great place to practice and improve technique, socialize with other badminton enthusiasts, or just hit around for fun. Players of all skill levels and experience - whether you're a curious beginner or a trained athlete - are welcome to join! Members may also try out for the team, which competes and consistently places in the upper divisions of regional tournaments, including the Yonex Northeast Collegiate Championships and Ivy League Badminton Tournament.

clubs.name: Brazilian Jiu Jitsu
clubs.description: The Columbia University Brazialian Jiu Jitsu Club has been home to thousands of students looking to stay safe, get in shape, and make new friends. Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu is a martial art focused on control and submission. Through a strong foundation based on positional hierarchy and body mechanics, it is designed to be the best means of gaining and maintaining control over a resisting opponent, while exposing opportunities for counter-attack. Combining the use of throws, takedowns, joint locks, chokes, and refined core body movement, the BJJ practitioner learns how to escape from an inferior position into a dominant one. It′s a lot of fun, great exercise, useful for self-defense, and an awesome way to challenge yourself and learn new things!

clubs.name: Columbia University Cheerleading
clubs.description:
Columbia University Cheerleaders have been a staple of Columbia spirit for several decades, assisting in the preservation of Columbia's rich tradition at campus events, football and basketball games. The cheerleaders also participate in community service events throughout the year.

Columbia University Cheerleaders have been a staple of Columbia spirit for several decades, assisting in the preservation of Columbia's rich traditions at campus events, football and basketball games as well as community service events.

clubs.name: Cycling
clubs.description:
Columbia University Cycling competes in collegiate and USCF races and is open to full time students of Columbia University.

The team is open to all full-time students at Columbia University - whether they be undergraduates or graduate students. Racing is primarily, but not limited to the road racing season which occurs in the Spring. CU cycling competes at 8-9 ECCC races as well as select USCF races.

Rob and Samantha Rowan (and Nate!) provide invaluable help running the team. The Rowans are volunteers who spend hundreds of hours each year on logisitics, fund raising, training and skills enhancement for the team's members. Samantha is a graduate of Barnard who came to cycling later in life. Rob is a USA Cycling certified Coach (level 3) and Official (category C).

clubs.name: Equestrian
clubs.description: The Columbia University Equestrian Club is comprised of recreational riders and show team riders. Show team riders compete against other collegiate teams as part of Zone 2 Region 4 of the Intercollegiate Horse Show Association (IHSA). Riders of all ability levels are welcome to participate in private and group lessons. Membership is open to undergraduate students, graduate students, and faculty of Columbia University with a Dodge Fitness Center membership.

clubs.name: Goju-Ryu Karate
clubs.description: Goju Ryu Karate is a martial arts club that has a little of everything. If you're interested in traditional punching and kicking or kata, we have that; if you want to learn throws, holds, and ground fighting, we do that too; if you want a cardio workout, sparring, or punching-bag drills, you're looking for us. We have a twenty-five year history of excelling at tournament. We go to the country for a weekend of intensive training. No matter your level, novice to master, we have something for you. It’s not just Karate; it’s a way of life.

clubs.name: Hiking
clubs.description: The Hiking Club is a voluntary club sport affiliated with Columbia University. We organize day hikes and camping trips throughout the year, mostly in the New York Tri-State area. Our officers will lead a few hikes per semester and then members suggest and lead the rest!

clubs.name: Ice Hockey (Men's)
clubs.description: The men's Columbia University College Ice Hockey team is a club sport that competes in the American Collegiate Hockey Association (ACHA) against teams throughout the Tri-State area. It is a competitive, full-contact league. Additionally the team competes in a weekend tournament against other Ivy League club teams. We welcome players of all skill levels. Graduate and undergraduate students are encouraged to contact us.

clubs.name: Ice Hockey (Women's)
clubs.description: The Women's Ice Hockey team is a club sport at Columbia that competes in the Delaware Valley Collegiate Hockey Conference (DVCHC) against teams from around the East Coast. Players of all skill levels, from novice to experienced players, piece together the team. The 2015-2016 team dominated the playoff tournament, leaving with a victory in the DVCHC championship. We welcome both undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, staff, and alumnae of all skill levels from Barnard College and Columbia University who have a Dodge Fitness Center membership. We look forward to seeing you on the ice!

clubs.name: Kayak
clubs.description: The Whitewater Kayaking team is a club sport at Columbia University that embarks on weekend whitewater kayaking excursions to rivers throughout the Northeast. During the week we host pool sessions at the Dodge Fitness Center to practice basic kayaking skills. This club is a great way to escape the city and enjoy the outdoors! Extra fun club activities include occasional camping during overnight river trips, our annual inter-collegiate competition at Dartmouth, and snowyaking in Riverside Park. We welcome students, faculty and staff from Columbia University and Barnard College who have a Dodge Fitness Center Membership and all levels of kayaking experience. Come even if you have literally zero experience. Seriously. Hope to see you at the pool!

clubs.name: Kendo
clubs.description: The Columbia Kendo Club promotes the practice of kendo, a Japanese martial art practiced with shinai (bamboo swords) and bogu (protective armor). We actively participate in intercollegiate tournaments and take promotion tests to earn higher ranks. Beginners are welcome to try out a couple of classes at any time, however you must be affiliated with Columbia University and have a Dodge Fitness Center membership in order to participate in the club. We will provide any necessary equipment initially, so come in whatever's comfortable.

clubs.name: Men's Lacrosse
clubs.description:
The CUMLC is a fast growing, competitive member of Columbia University's Club sports. We accept any and all players regardless of skill level as well as both undergraduate and graduate. Thanks to an allocation from CIF, we know have the funds to help newer players with helmets and gear.

 Come out and join us on the field or in the stands. Practices are twice a week at Columbia's Baker Athletics Complex, Tuesday and Thursday evening from 8:30-10:30pm. Buses leave at 8:00 and 8:15pm from 117th and Amsterdam.

clubs.name: Naginata
clubs.description: The Columbia University Naginata Club practices naginata, a Japanese halberd martial art that dates back to the Heian Period (794-1185 A.D.). We embrace both full-contact, armored sparring and choreographed forms in our practice. The club is a part of the Greater New York Naginata Federation (GNYNF) and competes locally and nationally with other dojos and regional federations. We welcome individuals of all experience levels who have a Dodge Fitness Center membership and are affiliated with Columbia University or Barnard College.

clubs.name: Road Runners
clubs.description: Columbia University Road Runners (CURR) aims to provide beginners and competitive runners with as many affordable racing opportunities, whether it be weekly NYRR races, local non-NYRR races, helping to cover NYC Marathon and NYC Half-marathon registration fees, to competing on our National Intercollegiate Running Club Association (NIRCA) team. NIRCA is an opportunity for members to travel to local universities and compete in cross country and track meets like a varsity team, without the high commitment and intensity. Members also may be seen capping off great group runs with brunch in various NYC restaurants. Being a member means you are a part of the rich running community at both CU and in NYC.

clubs.name: Rock Climbing
clubs.description: We are a group of adventurous undergraduate students, graduate students, alumni, faculty, and staff at Columbia University interested in all things rock climbing. The club welcomes and supports climbers of all levels, from first-time climbers to regional competition winners.

clubs.name: Rugby (Men's)
clubs.description: The Columbia University Men's Rugby Football Club (CURFC) competes in the Ivy League and Division 1 AA championships. The team had a successful spring season, where it finished 3rd amongst other schools in the 2017 Ivy League 7s tournament and is looking forward to a great fall season. The team welcomes all students of Columbia University interested in the great sport of rugby.

clubs.name: Rugby (Women's)
clubs.description: Columbia Women's Rugby competes in the Ivy Rugby Conference in the Fall playing fifteens-style rugby and in Spring against local teams in sevens-style rugby as well as attending the Ivy Rugby Tournament. We strive to be a constructive, intense, and bold team. Students from all of Columbia University's undergraduate colleges and of all athletic and sports experience are welcome to join!

clubs.name: Sailing
clubs.description: Open to both casual sailors and competing athletes, the sailing team encourages members to develop independence and self-confidence, improve communication, and foster teamwork and friendship while competing at the highest level of collegiate sailing. The sailing team is a club sport at Columbia University that competes with colleges and universities throughout the United States in the Intercollegiate Sailing Association (ICSA). The team draws members from all parts of the country and continues to uphold a tradition of sailing excellence year after year. Continually a competitive member of the Middle Atlantic Intercollegiate Sailing Association (MAISA), regattas take us from New Hampshire to Virginia, and everywhere in between. Practices are open to both undergraduate and graduate students from Columbia University and Barnard College who have a Dodge Fitness Center membership. All levels of sailing experience are welcome. As per ICSA rules, sailors that participate in weekend ICSA registered regattas must be undergraduates. Faculty and staff are welcome to volunteer.

clubs.name: Shotokan Karate
clubs.description: The Shotokan Karate Club's goal is to practice Shotokan Karate as a martial art at the highest level. We are affiliated with Shotokan Karate of America (SKA), a non-profit, non-commercial organization with more than 100 clubs around North America, as well as affiliates in 13 countries overseas. We attend several exchange practices at other universities each year and our members can even practice for free at other SKA-affiliated dojos while away from campus. Our practice involves physical and mental conditioning, self-defense, and, ultimately, becoming a better human being. The club community is very welcoming, and we are always working together to help each other learn and improve. We meet three times a week (Mon. 7-9 pm, Wed. 7-9 pm, and Sat. 10 am-12 pm), and members are welcome to come whatever day or days are easiest for them. We welcome Columbia University students, faculty, and staff of all experience levels who have a Dodge Fitness Center membership—to join us and challenge their minds and bodies.

clubs.name: Ski & Snowboard
clubs.description: The Columbia Ski Team is Columbia University's only skiing and snowboarding club. Also known as Columbia University Alpine Racing Team, CU Ski and Ride, Columbia Ski and Snowboard Club, Harlem Alpine Racing, or any combination of the above, the team provides a competitive environment for skiers and snowboarders to hone their skills on the racing slope and terrain park while fostering development among less advanced skiers and riders. Competitions, including Slalom, Giant Slalom, and Slopestyle, are run under the auspices of the US Collegiate Snowsport Association within the Mid-Atlantic Conference. With plenty of time to free-ski off the racing slope there's no limit on creativity. The team affords a fun social environment, providing the opportunity to make year-round relationships that may well last beyond graduation.

clubs.name: Table Tennis
clubs.description: As a member of the National Collegiate Table Tennis Association (NCTTA), the Columbia University Table Tennis Club competes in divisional, regional, and national tournaments. In 2015-2016, our coed team placed 11th in the country! But regardless of skill level, all individuals with a Dodge Fitness Center membership are welcome to join! Our goal is to foster a community at Columbia where we can all enjoy this fascinating sport.

clubs.name: Tae Kwon Do
clubs.description: Columbia University Tae Kwon Do (CUTKD) is the oldest and largest martial arts club on campus. Our team is made up of a diverse group of individuals brought together by our shared passion for taekwondo. We train together, compete together, and support one another in our endeavors to become better martial artists. We are tremendously proud of our club's growth and of our members' accomplishments, whether it be achieving their next belt rank or excelling in tournaments within the Eastern Collegiate Taekwondo Conference (ECTC) or the National Collegiate Taekwondo Association (NCTA).

clubs.name: Triathlon
clubs.description: Columbia Triathlon is a fun loving group that welcomes serious competitors to fitness enthusiasts who are affiliated with Columbia University and have a Dodge Fitness Center membership. We compete against colleges and universities throughout the Northeast, and love bonding over hard earned miles as well as good ole' fashioned fun. Last year our women's team won the Northeast Conference and our program as a whole sent four athletes to Collegiate Triathlon Nationals in Clemson, South Carolina. During the fall and spring semesters we have weekly practices in all three disciplines as well as get-togethers where we just kick back and relax on that all important rest day. Join us for the workouts, stay for the friendships, and do more than you ever thought possible!

clubs.name: Ultimate (Men's)
clubs.description: We are Uptown Local, Columbia University’s Men’s Ultimate Frisbee team and, since 1973, we have been practicing and competing in tournaments across the country. We strive to represent the core values of our sport and our university at the highest levels of competition, while never losing sight of our love for the game and each other. Ultimate is a team sport combining aspects of soccer, football, basketball and volleyball. Currently, it is one of the fastest growing sports in America; there are over 14,000 members in the college division alone. No experience is necessary to join. Most incoming first-year students join the team with little to no experience with competitive ultimate. The sport itself is young. The team is always changing. Interested players are always welcome.

clubs.name: Ultimate (Women's)
clubs.description: Columbia Women’s Ultimate is a D-1 club sport that welcomes students with all levels of Ultimate experience from any of Columbia's undergraduate and graduate schools. We seek to foster spirited play and build team chemistry on and off the fields. To accommodate students seeking varying levels of commitment and competition, we have an A team as well as a B team. Both teams compete against other colleges and universities along the East Coast. For the 2015-16 season, the A team finished 4th in the region and the B team placed 8th at its first Sectional appearance.

clubs.name: Volleyball (Men's)
clubs.description: The Columbia University Men's Volleyball Club is a student-run organization that competes as a Division I team in the New England Collegiate Volleyball League (NECVL). The team also participates in the National Collegiate Volleyball Federation (NCVF) national championship tournament. Regardless of skill level, we welcome students of all Columbia University undergraduate and graduate schools who have a Dodge Fitness Center membership. Practices are held throughout the academic year from 9pm-12am on Mondays and Thursdays in Levien Gymnasium.

clubs.name: Volleyball (Women's)
clubs.description: Columbia Women's Volleyball Club became an official club sport in the Fall of 2006. In the past, we have participated in the Northwest Women's Volleyball Club League (NWVCL), playing in tournaments against schools such as UCONN, Cornell, Yale, and Rutgers. This academic year, we hope to participate in the 2017 NCVF Club National Championships in Kansas City. We practice on Monday and Thursday nights from 9-11pm in Levien Gym, and our club welcomes students from all of the Columbia undergraduate and graduate schools who have a Dodge Fitness Center membership.

clubs.name: Water Polo (Women's)
clubs.description: The Columbia Women's Water Polo Club is committed to the development of sportsmanship, teamwork, and excellence. We are a diverse set of players from all skill levels and backgrounds, but we all hold one thing in common -- the love for our sport! Our team competes in the CWPA (Collegiate Water Polo Association) during the Spring season in various scrimmages and competitive tournaments with colleges in New York and across the Northeast. All individuals who are affiliated with Columbia University and have a Dodge Fitness Center membership are welcome to join us!

clubs.name: African Students Association
clubs.description: African Students Association provides a forum for the meaningful discussion of the political, social and cultural landscape of Africa, aiming to create a culturally enlightened community on campus by educating people about Africa.

clubs.name: Alianza
clubs.description: Alianza is a pan-Latinx student group that seeks to create a stronger Latinx community at Columbia University.

clubs.name: Asian American Alliance
clubs.description: The Asian American Alliance is a student organization that strives to promote understanding, foster dialogue and create a sense of awareness within the Asian Pacific Islander American community at Columbia University. It seeks to educate and address key issues that affect the APIA community at the University and beyond.

clubs.name: Asian/Pacific American Heritage Month
clubs.description: Columbia University Asian/Pacific American Heritage Month commits itself to organizing a wide range of programs for the month of April in order to bring broader awareness of the Asian American Pacific Islander American community and its rich history to Columbia's campus.

clubs.name: Black History Month (BHM)
clubs.description: Black History Month is a collaboration between Columbia University and Barnard College to increase awareness about Black issues and history.

clubs.name: Black Students Organization
clubs.description: Concerned with the recognition and understanding of the diverse needs of the African American community at Columbia University, the Black Student Organization prides itself on being a group that provides support, discussion and solutions to the University and greater New York City communities.

clubs.name: Brazilian Society
clubs.description: The Brazilian Society at Columbia University is the official student club for all who are fond of Brazil and would like to explore this country and its rich culture. It organizes major national events with renowned guest speakers, informal community-building activities and partnerships with other Latin American organizations.

clubs.name: Caribbean Students Association
clubs.description: Caribbean Students Association consists of students enrolled at Columbia University who identify with and/or are interested in the culture of the Caribbean. The group aims to foster a sense of unity and understanding among its members, their fellow students and the surrounding community through educational, cultural and social events.

clubs.name: ChicanX Caucus
clubs.description: Chicanx Caucus seeks to provide its members who self-identify as Chicanx, Mexican or Mexican-American with an environment that helps them fulfill their educational goals, promotes their cultural consciousness and advocates for them serving the needs of their community. The group's mission statement is to inform Chicanos from every region of the United States about higher educational opportunities.

clubs.name: Chinese Students Club
clubs.description: The Chinese Students Club of Columbia University is a non-profit, student-run organization that promotes social, cultural and political activities both on and off campus that aim to promote awareness of Chinese culture at Columbia.

clubs.name: Club Bangla
clubs.description: Club Bangla is a cultural group where both non-Bengalis and Bengalis from Bangladesh and the state of West Bengal in India can come together to celebrate the region's rich culture, heritage and language. Club Bangla also aims to create a platform for issues affecting Bengalis and the South Asian community at large.

clubs.name: Club Zamana
clubs.description: Club Zamana is the largest undergraduate South Asian organization at Columbia University and a functional umbrella for South Asian groups on campus.

clubs.name: Columbia Hellenic Society
clubs.description: The Columbia Hellenic Society is a community where native Greeks, diaspora Greeks, and Philhellenes can unite to discover and preserve the Hellenic culture at Columbia University. The e-board meets every other week to create and execute events centered around Greek holidays, foods, traditional dances, and the participation of our community with the overall general Hellenic community of New York. We try to have at least 2-3 events for our general board every month.

clubs.name: Columbia Iranian Students Association
clubs.description: Columbia Iranian Students Association is a non-political and non-religious organization open to people of all races and ethnicities. The purpose of this organization is to direct and organize meetings and events that promote Iranian culture and customs.

clubs.name: Columbia Por Colombia
clubs.description: Columbia PorColombia brings together students with a Colombian background and friends in the United States and Canada. It strives to establish partnerships and create valuable services for its members while forging countless ties within its communities.

clubs.name: Columbia Somali Student Association
clubs.description: Somali Students Association exists to meet the academic, social, and cultural needs of the Somali students at Columbia. It is also to promote unity amongst fellow Somalis, bring awareness of our diaspora's cultural heritage and history to both Somalis and non-Somalis, and play a positive role in the Somali community of New York City.

clubs.name: Columbia University Armenian Society
clubs.description: The objective of the Armenian Society of Columbia University is to unite all students of Armenian descent throughout the university. The organization is represented by students and alumni from around the world. The ASCU serves the Armenian community at large by promoting Armenian culture, heritage, and history through the organization of social, educational, and charitable events. The ASCU also networks with other Armenian and non-Armenian organization in effort to raise cultural awareness in our society.

clubs.name: Columbia University Asian Pacific American Heritage Month
clubs.description: Columbia University Asian/Pacific American Heritage Month commits itself to organizing a wide range of programs for the month of April in order to bring broader awareness of the Asian American Pacific Islander American community and its rich history to Columbia's campus.

clubs.name: CU Boricuas
clubs.description: CU Boricuas provides a safe and inclusive space for students who identify as Puerto Rican or strongly advocate for Puerto Rican causes, fostering an appreciation for the culture and engaging in vital social discussions. Moreover, CU Boricuas takes on the role of educating the broader Columbia community about Puerto Rico's intricate history, current affairs, and cultural heritage through academic and recreational activities, while also supporting grassroots non-profit organizations through fundraising initiatives.

clubs.name: Dar: The Palestinian Student Society
clubs.description: Dar: Palestinian Student Society is an undergraduate student group that serves to engage with and celebrate Palestinian culture, history, and identity. Through educational events and cultural programming, the society promotes awareness and dialogue on Palestinian issues within the campus and broader community.

clubs.name: Ethiopian and Eritrean Student Association
clubs.description: The Ethiopian and Eritrean Student Association is an organization committed to creating a support system for Columbia University students with an interest in Ethiopian and Eritrean cultures. The group fosters a community where Ethiopians and Eritreans can explore their cultures and traditions.

clubs.name: French Cultural Society
clubs.description: The French Cultural Society is a community of French students and Francophiles who explore French culture together.

clubs.name: Grupo Quisqueyano (GQ)
clubs.description: Grupo Quisqueyano is a student organization at Columbia University that represents Dominican students, heritage and culture on both Columbia University's and Barnard College's campuses and in the broader New York City community.

clubs.name: Hillel
clubs.description: Columbia/Barnard Hillel is the catalyst for students to explore and consciously define their Jewish identity. Its quest is to help students, regardless of their origin or destination, find their own interpretation of Jewish values, culture, community and religion. The group empowers students to grow intellectually, spiritually and socially.

clubs.name: Hindu Students Organization
clubs.description: Hindu Students Organization is an Indian cultural and Hindu organization founded in 1992. Throughout each year, the group hosts cultural celebrations and smaller events, building a tight-knit community.

clubs.name: Hong Kong Students and Scholars Society
clubs.description: The Hong Kong Students and Scholars Society is a Columbia University student interest group that aims to promote the culture of Hong Kong on campus.

clubs.name: Japanese Student Association (JSA)
clubs.description: Japanese Student Association (JSA) is an undergraduate organization of Columbia University, run by and composed entirely of students. Its purpose is to introduce and spread aspects of Japanese culture to the University community, bridging the gap between East and West.

clubs.name: Korean Students Association
clubs.description: Established in 1989, the Columbia University Korean Students Association is the representative Korean organization of Columbia University. The group's primary mission is to promote cultural and social events both on and off campus to celebrate Korea's rich heritage.

clubs.name: Latinx Heritage Month
clubs.description: Latino(a) Heritage Month is a collaboration between Columbia University and Barnard College. The organization strives to increase awareness about Latino and Latin American histories, identities, cultures, accomplishments and contemporary issues.

clubs.name: Liga Filipina
clubs.description: The purpose of Liga Filipina is to unify Columbia University students interested in Filipino culture through social interaction, cultural programs and activities, educational exchange and political awareness. It strives to promote this awareness of culture in the University community.

clubs.name: Mālama Hawai'i
clubs.description: Mālama Hawai'i is a Columbia University-run student organization dedicated to spreading Pacific Island and Polynesian culture. The group provides a safe space for students who identify as Pacific Islanders and for those who want to learn about the culture.

clubs.name: Muslin Afro Niyyah Students Association
clubs.description: Founded in 2018, the Muslin Afro Niyyah Students Association is Columbia and Barnard's first Black Muslim student group.

clubs.name: Native American Council
clubs.description: Native American Council strives to create a community for Indigenous students and their supporters in order to foster pride in identity, understanding of Indigenous issues, and relationships between Columbia University and Indigenous communities.

clubs.name: Native American Heritage Month
clubs.description: Native American Heritage Month provides the Columbia University community with programming regarding American Indian/Native American and Indigenous issues

clubs.name: Pakistani Student Association
clubs.description: The Columbia Pakistani Student Association was founded in 1992 with the hope of furthering diversity on the Columbia University Campus. PSA is Columbia University's space where students of Pakistani origin, as well as students interested in Pakistani culture, can form a community and socialize.

clubs.name: Polish Student Society at Columbia University
clubs.description: The Polish Student Society at Columbia University and Barnard College exists to promote greater understanding of Polish culture, public affairs, history and society throughout these academic communities.

clubs.name: Singapore Students Association (SSA)
clubs.description: The Columbia University Singapore Students Association aims to foster a sense of community for Singaporean students on Columbia's campus. The group also aims to enhance awareness of Singapore at the University through independent and collaborative events.

clubs.name: South East Asian League (SEAL)
clubs.description: Southeast Asian League is a forum where various Southeast Asian groups and students within the Columbia University community can come together, while also sharing cultural and social resources.

clubs.name: Student Organization of Latines (SOL)
clubs.description: Student Organization of Latines is a dynamic group dedicated to strengthening the Latinx/Latin American community and representing this heritage at Columbia University.

clubs.name: Taiwanese American Students Association
clubs.description: The Columbia Taiwanese American Students Association is an undergraduate organization dedicated to building a community for individuals interested in Taiwanese culture. It provides a home where people can also foster their interest in the Taiwanese American community, create life-long friendships and find inspiration from one another.

clubs.name: Thai Club
clubs.description: Thai Club at Columbia University was established to contribute to the appreciation of Thai culture and heritage. The purpose of Thai Club is also to provide a network support for Thai students.

clubs.name: The Sapna Project
clubs.description: The Sapna Project is a student group at Columbia University where students archive and explore the political, social and cultural facets of South Asian identity.

clubs.name: Turath
clubs.description: Turath is a nonpartisan undergraduate student association that serves to promote Arab culture at Columbia University. It aims to spread educational awareness about issues pertaining to the Arab world and celebrate the heritage of the Arab community.

clubs.name: Turkish Students Association
clubs.description:
Columbia Turkish Students Association is a student organization that brings together the Turkish community at Columbia University as well as introducing the Turkish culture to the general student body. We welcome all Columbia affiliates to reach out to us.

Every year, Columbia University accepts accomplished individuals from Turkey and from Turkish communities around the world to its undergraduate, graduate and post-graduate programs. Our goal is to provide a familial environment to these individuals who are united under Columbia’s roof.

Our mission is to foster an inclusive and welcoming environment of friendship among the students who self-identify as Turkish, as well as those who are interested in Turkish culture. We encourage everyone to join us and partake in our events. Feel free to reach out if you are interested in the Turkish culture. We will be more than happy to see you among us.

clubs.name: Venezuelan Student Association
clubs.description: The purpose of the Venezuelan Student Association at Columbia is to give the Venezuelan community on campus a space to feel represented as well as to share and celebrate our culture with other students who wish to learn more.

clubs.name: Vietnamese Students Association (VSA)
clubs.description: The Vietnamese Students Club of Columbia University is a student-run organization dedicated to promoting the rich Vietnamese heritage through social and cultural events both on and off campus.

clubs.name: Alpha Chi Omega
clubs.description: Alpha Chi Omega is devoted to reexamining and progressing the concepts of sisterhood and sorority. It advocates for domestic violence awareness and teaches women of all ages how to cultivate healthy relationships while also providing leadership and education opportunities.

clubs.name: Alpha Epsilon Pi
clubs.description: Alpha Epsilon Pi, the Jewish fraternity at Columbia University, includes a diverse group of young men who are involved in a variety of campus organizations including athletics, professional organizations, service groups and religious groups. The fraternity enjoys participating in campus intramural sports as well as philanthropic, social and community service events.

clubs.name: Alpha Kappa Alpha
clubs.description: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated, founded on the campus of Howard University in 1908, is the oldest Greek letter sorority established by Black women. The twenty visionary founders of Alpha Kappa Alpha sought to create a sorority that would cultivate and encourage high scholastic and ethical standards, promote unity and friendship among college women, study and help alleviate the problems concerning girls and women, maintain a progressive interest in college life, and to be of service to all mankind. Since her conception in 1908, Alpha Kappa Alpha has been dedicated to the pure fundamentals of Service to All Mankind. The Lambda Chapter of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated has served a pivotal role in the Harlem community since its chartering in 1922.

clubs.name: Alpha Omicron Pi
clubs.description: Alpha Omicron Pi Fraternity was founded in 1897 at Barnard College. The ideals of sincerity, service and friendship provide the foundation for the organization. The chapter promotes the values of simplicity, integrity, tolerance, generosity, personal dignity and love.

clubs.name: Alpha Phi Alpha
clubs.description: The Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. initially served as a study and support group for minority students who faced racial prejudice, both educationally and socially. As the African American fraternity at Columbia University, the organization promotes brotherhood and academic excellence while providing service and advocacy for its communities.

clubs.name: Delta Gamma
clubs.description: Delta Gamma is a Panhellenic sorority that provides a supportive community that aims to be an agent of change within the sorority system. Delta Gamma offers women of all ages experiences based on the principles of personal integrity, personal responsibility and intellectual honesty.

clubs.name: Delta Sigma Phi
clubs.description: Delta Sigma Phi is a values-based fraternity that seeks high-quality men who exemplify its ideals. As an open-minded organization, it supports cultural and religious diversity and recruits men who want to better themselves, the chapter and the community.

clubs.name: Delta Sigma Theta
clubs.description: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. is a sisterhood of over 250,000 predominately black college-educated women committed to public service. The Mighty Rho Chapter at Columbia University remains rooted in the sorority's legacy of sisterhood, scholarship and service for 95 years.

clubs.name: Gamma Phi Beta
clubs.description: Gamma Phi Beta is a Panhellenic sorority. Being a part of our chapter provides a support system of so many different women who help each other in countless ways. Gamma Phi Beta’s sisterhood is a place of love, support, warmth, kindness and encouraging each member to be the best person they can be.

clubs.name: Interfraternity Council
clubs.description: The Interfraternity Council (IFC) is the governing body of the 11 national fraternities at Columbia University. Led by its five executive board members, the council meets monthly with chapter presidents and representatives from each fraternity to discuss and vote on matters related to the council.

clubs.name: Intergreek Council
clubs.description: The Columbia University Inter-Greek Council oversees 29 fraternities and sororities on campus: 11 fraternities in the Interfraternity Council, six fraternities and six sororities in the Multicultural Greek Council, and six sororities in the National Pan-Hellenic Council.

clubs.name: Kappa Alpha Theta
clubs.description: Home to over 200 active members, the Epsilon Upsilon chapter of Kappa Alpha Theta is made up of leading women who strive for academic excellence and devote themselves to philanthropy and service. Kappa Alpha Theta was founded with the intention of providing a sisterhood for women who wanted to achieve their highest aspirations.

clubs.name: Kappa Delta Rho
clubs.description: Kappa Delta Rho is a lifetime brotherhood dedicated to the continuing character development of its members through its values: Fellowship, Leadership, Scholarship, Service and Tradition.

clubs.name: Kappa Phi Lambda
clubs.description: As the only Asian-interest sorority on campus, Kappa Phi Lambda has carved out a unique niche at Columbia University. The chapter maintains a significant presence both on- and off-campus by enhancing the cultural environment and by contributing to the community through service and philanthropy.

clubs.name: Lambda Phi Epsilon
clubs.description: Lambda Phi Epsilon is the first national Asian American interest fraternity and the first Asian American interest fraternity at Columbia University. The fraternity's motto is "To be Leaders Among Men," and its members strive to be leaders within the organization and community.

clubs.name: Lambda Pi Chi
clubs.description: The Beta Chapter of Latinas Promoviendo Comunidad/Lambda Pi Chi Sorority, Inc. was founded as the first Latina sorority at Columbia University.

clubs.name: Multicultural Greek Council
clubs.description: The Multicultural Greek Council is the student organization that oversees the many multicultural fraternities and sororities on campus. It is also one of the three Greek councils that make up the Inter-Greek Council.

clubs.name: Omega Phi Beta
clubs.description: Omega Phi Beta Sorority, Incorporated is a national sorority committed to the development of collegiate and professional women through sisterhood, diversity, leadership, service and academic excellence.

clubs.name: Order of Omega
clubs.description: Order of Omega is a national leadership honor society that recognizes fraternity women and men who have attained a high standard of scholarship, leadership and involvement.

clubs.name: Panhellenic Council
clubs.description: The Columbia University Pan-Hellenic Council oversees the six National Pan-Hellenic Conference sororities on Columbia's campus: Alpha Chi Omega, Alpha Omicron Pi, Delta Gamma, Gamma Phi Beta, Kappa Alpha Theta and Sigma Delta Tau. The council seeks to promote collaboration among individual chapters of the Greek system and to positively benefit the Columbia University community as a whole.

clubs.name: Phi Gamma Delta
clubs.description: Since its founding at Columbia University in 1866, the Omega Chapter of the Fraternity of Phi Gamma Delta (also known as Fiji) has remained committed its core values –– Friendship, Knowledge, Service, Morality and Excellence –– for recruiting the best men on campus.

clubs.name: Phi Iota Alpha
clubs.description: Membership in Phi Iota Alpha Latino Fraternity is a life-long commitment to Latin-American culture. It involves intellectual development, cultural consciousness, personal growth, personal achievement and social awareness.

clubs.name: Pi Delta Psi
clubs.description: As an Asian Fraternity, the mission of Pi Delta Psi is to maintain its fraternal existence by instilling values that nurture the continual development of the individual through Academic Achievement, Cultural Awareness, Righteousness, Friendship and Loyalty while fostering ethical behavior, leadership and philanthropy.

clubs.name: Sigma Chi
clubs.description: Sigma Chi is a lifelong brotherhood that strives to achieve true friendship, justice and fulfillment through learning.

clubs.name: Sigma Delta Tau
clubs.description: The Gamma Tau Chapter of Sigma Delta Tau was founded at Columbia University in 1992. It includes women from diverse backgrounds who are involved in activities all over New York City.

clubs.name: Sigma Lambda Beta
clubs.description: Sigma Lambda Beta is a Latino fraternity that strives to hold events that are not only enjoyable but also align with its principles of Brotherhood, Scholarship, Leadership, Cultural Awareness and Community Service.

clubs.name: Sigma Lambda Gamma
clubs.description: Sigma Lambda Gamma National Sorority, Inc. is a Latina sorority, which strives to be the premier organization committed to empowering all women.

clubs.name: Sigma Nu
clubs.description: The Delta Gamma Chapter of Sigma Nu was founded in 1908 at Columbia University and has had a long, celebrated history on campus. Sigma Nu remains dedicated to developing ethical leaders inspired by the principles of Love, Honor and Truth. The organization strives to foster the personal growth of each Columbia man's mind, heart and character, while creating lifelong friendships and commitment to the Fraternity.

clubs.name: Sigma Phi Epsilon
clubs.description: Sigma Phi Epsilon is rooted in the concept of Building Balanced Men. The fraternity's Balanced Man Program features a no-pledging, four-year experience focused on scholarship, leadership and life skills.

clubs.name: Zeta Beta Tau
clubs.description: Zeta Beta Tau Fraternity was founded in 1898 by a group of Jewish students and a Columbia University professor in New York City. The chapter was reestablished beginning in 2015, and its national organization welcomes members of all creeds and backgrounds while also being committed to no pledging and no hazing.

clubs.name: Zeta Phi Beta
clubs.description: Zeta Phi Beta was founded on the campus of Howard University on January 16, 1920. The Sorority's international programs such as Z-HOPE (Zetas Helping Other People Excel) through Mind, Body and Spirit serve to empower people from all walks of life. As the sorority celebrates its centennial year, it retains its original zest for excellence. It espouses the highest academic ideals and that has resulted in its members serving in groundbreaking roles in all fields of endeavor.

clubs.name: Columbia Mentoring Initiative
clubs.description: Columbia Mentoring Initiative (CMI) is an inter-generational mentorship program that connects first-year students (mentees) with returning students (mentors) and all students with alumni. In addition to program-wide events and activities for all participants, students have the opportunity to get involved in various "family trees" within the program.

clubs.name: Columbia Queer Alliance (CQA)
clubs.description: Columbia Queer Alliance (CQA) is the oldest queer collegiate student organization in the nation. CQA remains ever committed to fostering a cohesive, unified queer and trans community at Columbia University.

clubs.name: Columbia Queer and Asian (Q&A)
clubs.description: Q&A is a student group dedicated to creating a space for queer, genderqueer and trans Asian students, domestic and international. It hosts events and discussions focusing on the intersection of being queer and Asian, addresses the multitude of identities within the queer Asian community and provides support for all.

clubs.name: ColumbiAces
clubs.description: Columbia's Asexual and Aromantic student group, focusing on community and education.

clubs.name: First-Generation and/or Low-Income Network
clubs.description: Officially founded in Fall 2014 as Columbia First-Generation Low Income Partnership, Columbia FLI Network’s overall purpose is to provide appropriate communities and platforms for First-generation and low income students to talk about and act upon a range of issues that pertain to these intersectional identities.

clubs.name: GS Alliance
clubs.description: The GS Alliance is a group dedicated to the unique concerns and interests of the nontraditional student LGBTQIA+ community, welcoming students from all Columbia University schools and open to all orientations and gender identities. GS Alliance is a support group, social club and activists' haven.

clubs.name: IGNITE at Columbia
clubs.description: IGNITE at Columbia is a college chapter of a National nonpartisan organization. We are a collective of cis and trans women, as well as non-binary individuals, that are ready and eager to challenge structures of power, recognize our own role in perpetuating inequity, and do the hard work to ensure individuals and communities have access to the same opportunities, regardless of circumstances, identity, or experience.

clubs.name: Intercultural Resource Center
clubs.description: The Intercultural Resource Center (IRC) is devoted to promoting a just society and exploring intercultural and diversity issues within and beyond the Columbia University community. The IRC provides a forum for education and social exchange that encourages self-discovery, increased social awareness and an appreciation of the cultural histories within and between communities on campus. We strive to equip students, faculty and staff with the tools necessary to empower themselves, successfully navigate their environments and positively impact the community at large.

clubs.name: Jewish Women on Campus
clubs.description: Jewish Women on Campus (JWOC), a non-denominational community of women, comes together to learn, live, and empower each other in a purposeful space where everyone feels comfortable and foster a dialogue about womanhood and Judaism in the modern world through intellectual, social and religious events, including a performing arts show on campus exclusively for women and by women and Jewish Feminism Week.

clubs.name: JQ
clubs.description: JQ is the Jewish/LGBTQ+ community affiliated with Hillel. It offers monthly social gatherings and a safe space for students who share these identities to connect with each other.

clubs.name: Mixed Heritage Society
clubs.description: The Mixed Heritage Society of Columbia University is a campus organization that seeks to build community amongst students of two or more racial, ethnic or national backgrounds.

clubs.name: Proud Colors
clubs.description: Proud Colors is a group on Columbia University's campus that aims to implement a comprehensive action program to promote an understanding of the past, present and future experiences, problems and needs of queer and trans students of color, as well as the queer and trans community of color as a whole.

clubs.name: Queer Awareness Month (QuAM)
clubs.description: Queer Awareness Month is a collaboration between Columbia University and Barnard College to increase awareness about LGBTQ issues and history.

clubs.name: ROOTED
clubs.description: ROOTED (Respecting Ourselves and Others Through Empathy and Dialogue) is dedicated to creating spaces of solidarity, empathy, and learning for members of the Columbia community to explore identity, power, and privilege. Led by trained student facilitators, ROOTED hosts respectful and informed discussions about diversity and explores the commonalities and disparities among the social and political treatment of different groups in society. ROOTED facilitators lead open dialogues through the ROOTED Dinner & Dialogue series, plan an annual week centered on allyship, and work with student organizations, residences, and other constituencies to create tailored dialogue-based programming.

clubs.name: Students of Color Leadership Retreat
clubs.description: The Students of Color Leadership Retreat (SOCLR) is an annual retreat weekend that takes place during the fall semester in a residential camp setting. The SOCLR weekend is designed to fortify participants in their leadership at Columbia, Barnard and beyond, to focus on shared experiences, and to critically examine various issues and "isms" that relate to living in a multicultural and diverse community. Upon returning from the retreat, students are galvanized by the enhanced connections made during the weekend and are able to continue in their work as student leaders with a strong supportive community behind them. During the weekend, student leaders of color work on building their leadership skills using a developmental process.

clubs.name: US Milvets of CU
clubs.description: U.S. Military Veterans of Columbia University's mission is to provide military veterans with resources, opportunities and support. It aims to facilitate a successful education while also providing a strong foundation for years to come.

clubs.name: Voice in Sport at Columbia
clubs.description: Voice in Sport is an advocacy platform that connects and inspires female athletes. Voice in Sport Columbia is a university chapter that operates under the values of the larger organization. This group serves as a platform for female student-athletes to build a community through shared values and use their background and position in sports as a vehicle for change for themselves, each other, and their wider communities. The mission of the organization is to bring more visibility to female athletes and elevate their voices, as well as raise awareness around women’s equality within sports.

clubs.name: Women of Color Collective
clubs.description: Formerly known as Sister Circle prior to the Spring 2019 semester, Women of Color Collective (WOCC) was established in 2003 as a program that seeks to bring together self-identified Women of Color (including Arab/Middle Eastern, Asian/Pacific Islander, Black/African, Latinx, Native/Indigenous and Multiracial) to foster a sense of community and solidarity. We are open to the undergraduate and graduate students, faculty and staff of all Columbia University schools. Women of Color Collective has been instrumental in providing opportunities for self-identified women of color to connect with one another and examine personal, academic, professional and social challenges.

clubs.name: Womens History Month
clubs.description: The celebration of Women's History Month at Columbia College offers the University community opportunities to become better informed about important past events that have affected women and to examine the concepts that shape the ongoing understanding of women's history.

clubs.name: 4x4 Magazine
clubs.description: This student-run literary collective at Columbia University produces a printed magazine each spring and holds events, including open mic sessions, throughout the year.

clubs.name: Birch
clubs.description: Founded in 2004, The Birch Journal is the first national undergraduate publication devoted exclusively to Slavic, East European and Eurasian studies. The published issues are featured both online and in print, highlighting creative writing, literary criticism and essays on the culture and politics of the region.

clubs.name: Blue and White
clubs.description: The Blue and White is the monthly undergraduate magazine of Columbia University. It features award-winning investigative journalism, reviews, fiction, poetry, satire, art and more. Issues printed in signature blue ink are widely distributed throughout campus and Morningside Heights.

clubs.name: Bwog
clubs.description: Bwog is an independent, student-run campus news site. We publish content that is relevant to undergraduate students at the University, including breaking news; campus arts, science, and culture events; investigative features; and conspiracy theories – often packaged with a humorous voice. We also publish a weekly newsletter that packages these stories for subscribers.

clubs.name: Columbia Daily Spectator
clubs.description: Founded in 1877, the Columbia Daily Spectator delivers news daily to thousands of readers around Columbia University, Morningside Heights, West Harlem, and beyond. Content is published five days a week during the academic year, as well as in a weekly print edition, and offers news, arts, commentary, sports coverage, and photos from around campus and New York City, in conjunction with our blog, Spectrum, and our weekly arts and features magazine, The Eye. We are the second-oldest college daily paper in the country and have been financially independent from the University since 1962.

clubs.name: Columbia Economics Review
clubs.description: Founded in 2009 as the first undergraduate economics journal in the United States, the Columbia Economics Review (CER) aims to promote discourse and research at the intersection of economics, business, politics and society by publishing a rigorous selection of student essays, opinions and research papers in a print journal released each semester.

clubs.name: Columbia Journal of History
clubs.description: The Columbia Journal of History (CJH), formerly the Columbia Undergraduate Journal of History, is a publication of the Undergraduate History Council at Columbia University. The Journal was founded to provide opportunities for undergraduate students to contribute their research to the field of history. Our Executive Board reviews student submissions from history departments across the United States and abroad, and selects about 10% of submissions for inclusion in each biannual edition.

clubs.name: Columbia Political Review
clubs.description:
The Columbia Political Review is a multi-partisan, undergraduate magazine seeking to enhance involvement in the political process and to foster political discourse. As a multi-partisan organization, CPR does not endorse the ideas contained within its pages, although it is dedicated to presenting unique vantages on political situations, cast through the Columbia and collegiate lenses.

The Review includes everything from movie and book reviews with a political slant to in-depth features on politics ranging from the local to the global.

clubs.name: Columbia Review
clubs.description: The Columbia Review is published twice a year and is available free on the Columbia campus and on the magazine's website. The magazine does not specialize in the work of any particular gender, ethnic group or University division. The Review also accepts and publishes submissions from writers and artists not affiliated with Columbia University.

clubs.name: Columbia Undergraduate Journal of Global Health (JGH)
clubs.description: The Journal of Global Health (JGH) is an international public health publication and media organization based at Columbia University that's committed to featuring original student research and spotlighting activism in the field.

clubs.name: Columbia: A Journal of Literature and Art
clubs.description: Columbia is a journal of literature and art, which prides itself on variety in the issues it produces and the writers it includes. The magazine is edited by a team of writers with a keen eye for quality new writing and a strong sense of what they want to see in a journal.

clubs.name: Echoes
clubs.description: Echoes is the only literary magazine of Barnard College. Based out of New York City, we are the voice of the women who make up our community and are dedicated to serving as a platform for students to share their work in literary and visual arts. Submissions of all forms of writing and art are considered and successful entries are compiled into a hard-copy magazine which is released bi-yearly.

clubs.name: Federalist Paper
clubs.description: The Federalist is Columbia University’s satirical newspaper, which includes students of all academic backgrounds and comedic experience.

clubs.name: Ferris Reel Film Society
clubs.description: Ferris Reel Film Society is a student-run club that organizes free movie screenings on- and off-campus all year for the Columbia University student body.

clubs.name: Gadfly
clubs.description: The Gadfly is the undergraduate philosophy magazine of Columbia University, which publishes academic papers, interviews, events and free-form work.

clubs.name: Grey Matters CU
clubs.description: Grey Matters is Columbia's chapter of the Grey Matters undergraduate neuroscience publication. Our mission is to enhance public understanding of neuroscience, to encourage greater participation in the scientific community, and to develop skilled science communicators via collaborative publications.

clubs.name: GYNECA
clubs.description: GYNECA is a semesterly intercollegiate journal publishing undergraduate peer-reviewed research in all fields of gynecology and gender minority healthcare on the basis of its originality, importance, interdisciplinary interest, timeliness, accessibility, elegance and surprising conclusions. GYNECA also provides rapid, authoritative, and insightful news and interpretation of topical and coming trends affecting science, scientists and the wider public.

clubs.name: Hoot Magazine
clubs.description:
Hoot Magazine was founded in 2009 by a group of fashion obsessed students at Columbia University. 

We cover fashion, art, and culture in New York City, and produce original content that reflects New York's vibrant personality. Open to the entire Columbia community, the publication provides members with the opportunity to lend their skills and demonstrate their talent in writing, photography, styling, hair, makeup, web design, editing, layout, and public relations among others

clubs.name: Journal of Literary Criticism
clubs.description: Founded in 2002 by undergraduate English majors, the Columbia Journal of Literary Criticism acts as an interdisciplinary forum centered around literature, culture and politics. The journal is published once a year and includes articles, reviews, interviews and original artwork.

clubs.name: Postcrypt Art Gallery
clubs.description: Postcrypt Art Gallery is a collaborative gallery at Columbia University, with pop-up shows and openings curated by students.

clubs.name: Quarto
clubs.description: Quarto is the official undergraduate literary magazine of Columbia University’s Creative Writing Department. It is a student-run magazine that publishes the best of Columbia’s undergraduate writers from all four of Columbia’s undergraduate colleges. The Creative Writing Department provides support and a faculty advisor to the magazine, though the editorial board has representatives from a variety of academic fields across campus.

clubs.name: RATROCK
clubs.description: RATROCK is the undergraduate arts publication of Columbia University.

clubs.name: Science Review
clubs.description: The Columbia Science Review is a student-led publication group that strives to increase scientific literacy and awareness in the Columbia University community and beyond.

clubs.name: Undergraduate Law Review
clubs.description: The goal of the Columbia Undergraduate Law Review is to provide Columbia University and the public with an opportunity to discuss law-related ideas and to publish undergraduate legal scholarship.

clubs.name: Undergraduate Science Journal
clubs.description: The Columbia Undergraduate Science Journal is a professional-level, open-access science journal that is committed to publishing manuscripts of the highest scholarship resulting from significant scientific research or outstanding scientific analysis.

clubs.name: WKCR
clubs.description: WKCR-FM, Columbia University’s non-commercial student-run radio station, is dedicated to presenting a spectrum of alternative programming: traditional and art music, spoken arts and original journalism.

clubs.name: Yearbook
clubs.description: The Columbian is the official yearbook for Columbia College, Columbia Engineering and the School of General Studies.

clubs.name: Bach Society
clubs.description: The Columbia Bach Society Orchestra and Chorus is the only student-run orchestra and choir at the University dedicated to classical music, community building and student leadership. Composed of Columbia University students as well as young musicians from the greater New York City community, the Bach Society presents several concerts throughout the academic year.

clubs.name: Barnard/Columbia Flute Choir
clubs.description: We are Columbia's only flute-only performance group!

clubs.name: Classical Performers
clubs.description: Columbia Classical Performers gives musicians an outlet where they can share their music with the public and provides the Columbia community with free, high-quality classical music. The group provides on- and off-campus venues, coordinates recital logistics, publicizes events and plans post-concert receptions.

clubs.name: Clefhangers
clubs.description: The Columbia Clefhangers (aka "Clefs") are students at the University who form a contemporary coed a cappella group in New York City. Since 1988, the Clefs have been singing from Rockefeller Center to Paris, entertaining audiences with their original arrangements of pop, R&B and soulful music of every genre.

clubs.name: Columbia Chinese A Cappella
clubs.description: Columbia Chinese A Cappella is Columbia's first Chinese a cappella group, with members from multiple schools within Columbia who joined because of their love for Chinese pop music and culture. Through this unique style of music, we hope to spread our passion for Chinese music and culture to everyone else in the Columbia community and inspire others to join in.

clubs.name: Columbia Chinese Orchestra
clubs.description: Student-run Chinese orchestra at Columbia University. CCO holds regular concerts and performances each semester, and provides a space for members to learn about traditional Chinese orchestral music, practice together, and perform.

clubs.name: Columbia Composers
clubs.description: Columbia Composers is a student-run organization supporting the creation and performance of new works by graduate students enrolled in Columbia University’s Doctoral Composition Program. Each year we organize four or five concerts in various venues throughout New York City, attracting a mix of student and outside attendees thereby broadening the visibility of our composers both individually and collectively. We have collaborated with such ensembles as the International Contemporary Ensemble (ICE), JACK quartet, Talea, Wet Ink, Yarn/Wire, and many New York freelance musicians. Our activities are made possible by the generous support of the Alice M. Ditson and the Fritz Reiner Funds.

clubs.name: Columbia Pops
clubs.description: Columbia Pops is a student-run organization with the goal to engage students not only as performance artists but also as conductors, arrangers, leaders and much more. Columbia Pops welcomes members from all four undergraduate schools. The ensemble boasts a diverse group of talented musicians and is committed to performing student arrangements alongside published works.

clubs.name: CU Pep Band
clubs.description: The Columbia Pep Band (CU Pep Band) is Columbia's premier student ensemble that performs at Columbia Athletics events. Established in 2022, CU Pep Band has brought energetic music and school spirit to Columbia football games including Homecoming and basketball games including the Ivy League Basketball Tournament. The band's repertoire includes Columbia's iconic fight song "Roar, Lion, Roar!" as well as classic marching band tunes and popular song arrangements. Since its inception, CU Pep Band has been under the direction of Brent Morden, Columbia College alum and former CU Wind Ensemble President. The band welcomes all winds, brass, and percussion players regardless of skill level and is actively recruiting.

clubs.name: CU Records
clubs.description: CU Records is a student-run recording studio at Columbia University. Its goal is to foster the campus music scene by serving individual musicians and acts that do not possess the resources to record or showcase their own music.

clubs.name: CU Sur
clubs.description: SUR is Columbia University's premier South Asian fusion a cappella group. The group brings together South Asian and Global music through its arrangements and performances.

clubs.name: Jubilation!
clubs.description: Jubilation! is Columbia University’s Christian a cappella group. Founded in 1990, the group aims to be a unified body that uses its talents to glorify God and bring joy to others.

clubs.name: Kingsmen
clubs.description: The Kingsmen are Columbia University's premier all-male a cappella group. Including 12 highly talented, motivated young men, the group features a repertoire of barbershop, gospel, traditional school songs, Christmas tunes, contemporary selections and some witty songs that they wrote themselves.

clubs.name: Metrotones
clubs.description: Founded in 1983, the Columbia Metrotones are Columbia University’s premier all-female a cappella group. It performs at a wide variety of venues and events in and outside of New York City.

clubs.name: Nonsequitur
clubs.description: Nonsequitur is Columbia’s premier co-ed a cappella group and has performed most recently at Lincoln Center and Battery Park. Boasting musical alums like Tony and Grammy-Award winning Ben Platt, they will be appearing on a new HBO show, and their most recent album, “But We Do,” is available on all streaming platforms.

clubs.name: Notes and Keys
clubs.description: Founded in 1908, Notes and Keys is Columbia University's oldest and finest co-ed a cappella group with a diverse and constantly expanding repertoire of skillfully written arrangements by their own members. They have performed on VH1, at NYC's Knickerbocker Club, Yankee Stadium, Dylan's Candy Bar, the United Nations, Gracie Mansion and at Lin-Manuel Miranda's apartment.

clubs.name: Pizmon
