clubs.description: Pizmon, the co-ed, pluralistic Jewish a cappella group of Columbia, Barnard, and JTS, is a non-profit organization that uses Jewish music to connect to and inspire communities around the globe through both domestic and international travel throughout the academic year.

clubs.name: Postcrypt Coffee House
clubs.description: Postcrypt Coffeehouse is an all-acoustic music venue in the basement of St. Paul's Chapel at Columbia University, run completely by students.

clubs.name: S'madar
clubs.description: S’madar, the all-women’s Jewish a capella group of Columbia, Barnard, and JTS, aims to provide an active musical presence for the Jewish community by performing regularly both on campus and in nearby communities.

clubs.name: SHARP
clubs.description: Officially founded in 2011, Sharp is Columbia University’s newest all male a cappella group. It prides itself on a commitment to producing outstanding musical experiences for audiences both on and off campus.

clubs.name: Uptown Vocal
clubs.description: Uptown Vocal (originally the Catatonics) was founded in 1991 as a co-ed a cappella group at Columbia University. It performs jazz and pop songs for the campus community.

clubs.name: Wind Ensemble
clubs.description: The Columbia University Wind Ensemble consists of woodwind, brass and percussion players who perform pieces of various instrumentation and styles. It offers free concerts to the University community and also hosts the Columbia Festival of Winds, an all-day concert that raises money for the music education program Musical Mentors Collaborative.

clubs.name: Barnard Columbia Ancient Drama Group
clubs.description: Every spring the Barnard and Columbia Classics departments jointly produce an ancient Greek or Latin play in the original language. Under the guidance of Professor Helene Foley (Barnard College), graduate and undergraduate students, faculty members, and friends of the departments work together to bring an ancient text to life.

clubs.name: Bhangra
clubs.description: Founded in 2002, Columbia University Bhangra is a competitive collegiate dance team, committed to fostering an appreciation of Punjab culture in both its dancers and audiences alike.

clubs.name: Black Theatre Ensemble
clubs.description: The Columbia University Black Theatre Ensemble creates theatre productions each fall and spring with and for the black community at Columbia University and New York City at large. The group seeks to promote playwrights, actors and theatre artists of color, providing an outlet for creative expression within these communities.

clubs.name: Chowdah Sketch Comedy Troupe
clubs.description: Chowdah is the premier sketch comedy group on the campus of Columbia University. It performs regularly and all material is original and written by members of the group.

clubs.name: CoLab Performing Arts Collective
clubs.description:
CoLab is an interdisciplinary student art group at Columbia University. We value collaboration and the creative process. CoLab is made up mostly of dancers and choreographers, but we love to incorporate art of all disciplines into our showcases. Past performances have included live music, visual art, photography, film, spoken word, and more.

CoLab presents one showcase each semester. We hold work-in-progress showings leading up to each performance. This gives our members an opportunity to receive peer feedback on their work, and see what others have created.

clubs.name: Columbia Ballet Collaborative
clubs.description: Columbia Ballet Collective is committed to enriching the arts at the University and providing a platform for collaboration between professionals in the community and Columbia University students.

clubs.name: Columbia Ballroom Dance Team
clubs.description:
We are the premier ballroom dance organization at Columbia University, and we do everything we can to support our members in their dance journeys.

We offer classes and workshops, practice space, a one-on-one mentorship program, and the opportunity to compete. We are a fun-loving, social group that welcomes all new members — no partner or prior dance experience necessary to join!

clubs.name: Columbia China Dance
clubs.description: CU China Dance was founded with the mission of performing authentic Chinese traditional dances that represent its diverse culture, while enriching people's knowledge about China at Columbia University and in New York City.

clubs.name: Columbia Musical Theatre Society
clubs.description: The Columbia Musical Theatre Society produces high-quality musical revivals by striving to model the collaborative process of professional musical theatre and foster an inclusive, positive experience for all. As a community, CMTS endeavors to offer continuing mentorship and guidance to student theatre artists of all backgrounds, schools, and majors.

clubs.name: Columbia Repertory Ballet (CRB)
clubs.description: Columbia Repertory Ballet was created to give dancers at Columbia opportunities to learn and perform repertoire (existing works) from the classical ballet canon as well as from contemporary ballets in a professional rehearsal setting. Our dancers range from pre-professional dancers (seriously trained dancers throughout high school) to current and retired professional ballet dancers. Columbia University attracts so many talented ballet dancers and we wanted to give our members the ability to keep their dancing passions alive in addition to their diverse academic pursuits.

clubs.name: Columbia SLAM! Poetry
clubs.description: SLAM! is Columbia University’s only recreational Spoken Word club. We aim to forge a safe, dynamic, and collaborative space for poetry lovers to come together and create. We design and host workshops and events to foster both written poetry skills and performance — all levels of experience are welcome!

clubs.name: Columbia University Ballet Ensemble
clubs.description: Columbia University Ballet Ensemble, or, as we endearingly call it, CUBE, fills the classical ballet niche in the university's dance community. Each semester, CUBE gives ballet dancers of all level on campus the opportunity to learn, rehearse, and perform classical and dramatic roles, producing a work based on one story ballet in a fun and challenging, yet supportive environment.

clubs.name: Columbia University Dance Team
clubs.description: The Columbia University Dance Team performs various types of dance including pom, jazz, and hip-hop at Football and Men and Women's Basketball. Our main focus is to support Columbia athletic teams and provide engaging entertainment at school events.

clubs.name: Columbia University Swing Dance Club
clubs.description: Columbia University Swing Dance Club exists to unify the swing dance community of Columbia University. Strong ties with America's unique sub-culture of jazz music and movement allow us to promote the dance as an exciting social endeavor. The CU Swing Dance Club is dedicated to providing events and instruction in Lindy Hop, Balboa, and Charleston. Our members organize and attend events throughout New York City.

clubs.name: Control Top!
clubs.description: Possibly the most influential, cross-genre Barnard-based six person girl group of our generation, Control Top's laugh-based approach to laughter and dedication to shamelessness, demonstrates a unmatched commitment to the founding principle of American feminism: Funny Women Kick Ass! In a world where every shiny-toothed 15 year old has won a kids choice award for making jokes about pajamas on the Disney Channel, fans are crying out for the rawness and sheer power of a performance group that will break all the rules (while still wearing excellent outfits). A ticket to a Control Top show is often literally priceless, making them the most exclusive and, arguably, sought-after gurlprov group on the planet.

clubs.name: CU Generation
clubs.description: Columbia University (CU) Generation is an urban collegiate dance team / family founded in 2010. With its roots in Asian culture, the group has since evolved to encompass a wide range of choreography and music. CU Generation aims to help promote the urban dance community and provide a shared, inclusive space for its members to grow and support one another.

clubs.name: CU Players
clubs.description: CU Players is Columbia’s premier student-run theater group on campus. CU Players offers many opportunities to join the Columbia University theater community and includes students of all experience levels.

clubs.name: CU Raqs Sharqi
clubs.description: CU Raqs Sharqi is a group of students dedicated to exploring the ancient art of Middle Eastern dance. The group performs traditional Egyptian, Turkish, American Cabaret and Tribal Fusion styles.

clubs.name: CU Sketch Show
clubs.description: CU Sketch Show is Columbia University's first and only video sketch comedy club. It was founded in 2014 and has been producing videos weekly on YouTube ever since.

clubs.name: CU Taiko
clubs.description: Columbia University (CU) Taiko is a group dedicated to the practice of Japanese taiko drumming. CU Taiko is open to all members of the Columbia University community. It serves as a medium through which students can explore and promote Japanese/Japanese-American culture, heritage and art.

clubs.name: Film Production
clubs.description: Columbia Undergraduate Film Productions is an undergraduate film club at Columbia University. Its activities include making films, renting free film equipment, helping people with their own films outside of the group and putting on a film festival at the end of each year featuring only Columbia University student filmmakers.

clubs.name: Fruit Paunch
clubs.description: Fruit Paunch is Columbia University's oldest improv comedy troupe, which has developed its own style of long-form improv, "Unplugged."

clubs.name: Ijoya
clubs.description: Ijoya’s purpose is to educate the Columbia community about African Dances and African-rooted Dance styles and celebrate the centuries of history of African and Afro-Caribbean dances. We hope to teach people about the African dance from centuries ago to modern Afrobeats today.

clubs.name: Kings Crown Shakespeare Troupe
clubs.description: King's Crown Shakespeare Troupe of Columbia University is a not-for-profit group providing free shows on campus.

clubs.name: LateNite Theatre
clubs.description: LateNite Theatre maintains a fifteen-year commitment to the Columbia/Barnard playwright community. We have a simple purpose: to offer our playwrights the opportunity to see their work on stage, giving them a freedom to experiment, to take artistic risks, and above all, to have fun in a non-competitive environment. Each semester, we bring to life an anthology of new student-written works with these goals in mind.

clubs.name: Lion Dance
clubs.description: Columbia University Lion Dance performs a high-energy dance form based on kung fu. Its goal is to promote knowledge of Chinese traditional dance for both the on-and off-campus community.

clubs.name: Memento Mori
clubs.description: Columbia University's stand up comedy group.

clubs.name: New Opera Workshop
clubs.description:
New Opera Workshop (NOW) offers Columbia University students the opportunity to perform and produce opera in a collaborative, student-led workshop setting. NOW entertains the Columbia University community with high-quality productions appropriate for young voices, while helping members gain the skills necessary for careers in the modern world of opera. NOW enriches the operatic art form by developing new music and performance practices in order to engage new audiences.

NOW is proud to be recognized by the Governing Board of Barnard and a member of the Columbia University Performing Arts League. NOW's executive board, creative teams, and performers are all Columbia University students. All our proceeds are used to produce NOW's shows.

clubs.name: NOMADS
clubs.description: NOMADS produces original student-written theatre each semester, and is one of only two clubs at Columbia University that presents student-writing for the stage. From playwrights and composers, to actors, directors, designers, and technicians, NOMADS is dedicated to fostering artistic growth and collaboration among Columbia University theatre artists. Through producing and developing original student theatrical works, we aim to encourage emerging theatre artists to explore their creativity and develop their own particular crafts for the stage. We seek to present challenging, entertaining, and thought-provoking material for audiences at Columbia and in the wider New York theatre world. In addition to full productions, NOMADS programs include: The NOMADS Theatre Workshop and The PlayPen.

clubs.name: Onyx Dance Troupe
clubs.description: ONYX is Columbia University's elite pre-professional hip-hop group. The members perform on and off campus, utilizing a variety of different dance styles in their choreography.

clubs.name: Orchesis
clubs.description: Orchesis is Columbia University's largest performing arts group with completely student-run activities, including production, choreography and dancing. A performance showcase is presented every semester, and the group welcomes all levels of dancers.

clubs.name: Performing Arts League
clubs.description: As an umbrella organization, the Columbia University Performing Arts League facilitates discussion among groups in the Columbia University arts community, encourages the sharing of resources among groups and serves as an advisory board to any newly formed performing arts groups or special projects.

clubs.name: Raas
clubs.description: Columbia Raas was established in the fall of 2003 to celebrate the tradition and energetic dance style of Garba-Raas. The group performs at various venues both on and off campus and competes in Garba-Raas competitions across the nation.

clubs.name: Raw Elementz
clubs.description: Raw Elementz is the largest hip-hop dance crew at Columbia University that is well-known for crowd-pleasing performances at both on- and off-campus events including cultural shows, athletic events, promotional events and community service.

clubs.name: Sabor
clubs.description: Sabor is Columbia University's first Latino dance troupe. Established in 2003, Sabor performs salsa, bachata, merengue and many other styles of dance.

clubs.name: Shalhevet Dance Troupe
clubs.description: Shalhevet, the Israeli dance troupe on campus, shares the joy of both traditional and modern Israeli folk dance through learning dances and performing, no matter your dance experience!

clubs.name: Taal
clubs.description: The fundamental intent of Taal is to promote awareness of South Asian dance, Indian culture and the arts. The team performs in competitions and performance showcases, and is open to all members of the Columbia University/Barnard College community.

clubs.name: Third Wheel Improv
clubs.description: Third Wheel Improv is a co-ed improv comedy group at Columbia/Barnard that does both long-form and short-form improv, hosts an annual improv festival and a weekly open rehearsal.

clubs.name: Untapped
clubs.description: UnTapped is Columbia University's tap dancing group, dedicated to enriching campus through the art of tap.

clubs.name: Varsity Show
clubs.description: The Varsity Show, founded in 1894, is one of the oldest traditions at Columbia University, and certainly its oldest performing arts tradition. Each year, the Varsity Show attracts some of Columbia University and Barnard College’s finest actors and creative talents.

clubs.name: Wushu
clubs.description: Founded in 2010, Columbia Wushu has grown to become the largest collegiate Chinese martial arts club in the New York City area, welcoming a large family of practitioners from all backgrounds, ages, levels of experience and walks of life.

clubs.name: American Enterprise Institute @ Columbia (AEI)
clubs.description: American Enterprise Institute @ Columbia provides substantive conversations about public policy on campus by hosting events and activities throughout the year.

clubs.name: Amnesty International
clubs.description: Founded as the Columbia and Barnard chapter of Amnesty International, the organization seeks to keep the Columbia University community informed about human rights violations around the world and to promote student action through letter-writing, hosting speakers, facilitating discussions, fundraising and building colations with other student groups.

clubs.name: Aryeh
clubs.description: Aryeh is Columbia University’s pro-Israel public affairs committee that aims to engage the campus community about Israel by providing Columbia students with diverse opportunities to connect with Israel including cultural, academic, political, and philanthropic programming

clubs.name: Barnard-Columbia Socialists
clubs.description: Barnard-Columbia Socialists is a group of students, workers and other members of the University community who agree on the need to organize against all forms of exploitation and oppression. The group aims to fight for and build a socialist alternative that puts people before profits.

clubs.name: College Democrats
clubs.description: Columbia University Democrats is one of the largest undergraduate political organizations on campus. It aims to promote progressive causes, discuss issues and plan activism on campus, in New York City and across the country.

clubs.name: College Republicans (CUCR)
clubs.description: The Columbia University College Republicans publishes and promotes the ideas and positions of the Republican Party, while fostering community and providing support for Republican students on campus.

clubs.name: Columbia EcoReps
clubs.description:
Columbia University EcoReps is a group of students working in collaboration with Columbia’s offices of Housing, Dining, and Environmental Stewardship to promote sustainable behavior and implement green initiatives on Columbia’s campus.

 

EcoReps was founded in 2005 by a team of students and administrators from the Offices of Housing, Dining and Student Services. The brainchild of various offices under the leadership of Scott Wright, Vice-President of Campus Services, and a group of students led by Six Silberman and Coogan Brennan to create sustainable activism, policy, and infrastructure on Columbia’s campus. They were paid employees of Housing and Dining, serving as residence hall representatives seeking to increase the amount of sustainable living education to students through outreach and initiatives like reducing each building’s energy consumption and increasing the recycling rate in particular floors. Each EcoRep would be assigned a particular dormitory and the group would meet to outline specific projects. In 2009-2010 EcoReps coordinators re-imagined the organization as a functional student group without monetary compensation or residence hall assignment due to the strain it put on the members. Split up into various committees, beginning with Food and Water, Energy, Waste and Recycling, and ECO’s (the revamped version of the earlier residence hall format), the EcoReps increased their programming, recruitment, and impact on campus. Today, the EcoReps are comprised of about 50 active student members organized into Dining, Recycling, and Living Green committees.

clubs.name: Columbia European Society
clubs.description: The Columbia European Society is the only University­-wide society that brings together students interested in Europe and European affairs through lectures, workshops, conferences and more.

clubs.name: Columbia Lions for Life
clubs.description: Columbia Lions for Life is a secular student advocacy organization that seeks to create constructive dialogue around life issues on Columbia University's campus.

clubs.name: Columbia One for the World
clubs.description: One for the World Columbia is a student-run philanthropy group founded in Spring 2017 as a constituent part of One for the World, with the express goal of combating extreme poverty in the developing world.

clubs.name: Columbia Policy Institute
clubs.description: The Columbia Policy Institute is a progressive, nonpartisan, student-run think tank. The student group releases a yearly undergraduate policy journal, hold weekly policy discussions, and host events with elected officials, policy professionals and Columbia faculty. Students support advocacy projects in a wide range of policy centers including human rights, economic development, education, energy & environment, technology, healthcare and democratic access. A bi-annual trip to Washington D.C. is also organized.

clubs.name: Columbia Political Union (CPU)
clubs.description: Founded in 1935, the Columbia Political Union is organized for and by the students of Columbia University. It seeks to enhance involvement in the political process, domestic and international, and draw every member of the campus community into an ongoing discussion of political ideas.

clubs.name: Columbia Public Health Club
clubs.description: As a group, the Columbia Public Health Club's keystone objective is to identify and research health inequities within nearby communities and implement a yearlong project to lessen the impact of these inequalities.

clubs.name: Columbia Students for Global Health Equity and Medicine (GHEM)
clubs.description: Founded in 2008, GlobeMed at Columbia is one of 46 GlobeMed chapters working to improve the health of people living in poverty around the world. It partners with Gulu Women’s Economic Development and Globalization, a human rights organization based in Gulu, Uganda, to provide health services, economic empowerment, psychosocial support and human rights advocacy for the communities surrounding Gulu.

clubs.name: Columbia Synapse
clubs.description: Columbia Synapse is a New York City-based service organization guided by principles of neuroscience, community, and advocacy for the community of individuals with brain injury and other invisible disabilities. The group draws on a wide network of resources from the City’s hospital systems to organize a diverse portfolio of programs that cultivate a community for individuals with acquired brain injury (ABI) and a greater understanding of brain injury for Columbia University and New York City. We partner with major stakeholders including international non-profits, state agencies and the New York Mayor's Office of People with Disabilities.

clubs.name: ColumbiaVotes
clubs.description: ColumbiaVotes aims to assist students in registering to vote and requesting absentee ballots.

clubs.name: Doctors Without Borders Student Chapter at Columbia University
clubs.description: The “Doctors Without Borders” Student Chapter at Columbia University is an interdisciplinary organization dedicated to advocacy and the principles of humanitarian medicine. We aim to advance medical ethics and improve access to healthcare. In our chapter we will advocate for and support a variety of humanitarian crises, such as refugee interests, minority and women’s rights, environmental justice, mental health, and more, both on and off campus.

clubs.name: GendeRevolution
clubs.description: GendeRevolution (GendeRev/GR) is the trans support and advocacy group of Columbia University and Barnard College. It aims to create safe spaces and advocacy for trans and queer people on campus while raising awareness of the variety of trans identities and experiences. GendeRevolution embraces an intersectional approach to social justice.

clubs.name: J Street CU
clubs.description: J Street CU is part of a student-driven network of Pro-Israel, Pro-Palestine, Pro-peace activists organizing on campuses across North America for peace, security and social justice in Israel, the future state of Palestine and across the Middle East.

clubs.name: Jewish Activist Collective
clubs.description: The Jewish Activist Collective is a group meant to bring together both conversation and action around social issues. We believe it is our Jewish imperative to seek justice and pursue it. As part of JAC one will be able to take the time to learn and understand a cause, participate in some form of text-based learning to give a Jewish backbone to our action, and participate in a form of action where we will be walking along as allies.

clubs.name: Planned Parenthood Generation at Columbia
clubs.description: Planned Parenthood Generation at Columbia University is a student-run organization that advocates for sexual health and education.

clubs.name: Platypus Marxist Reading Group (Columbia Platypus)
clubs.description: A Marxist reading group.

clubs.name: Scientists and Engineers for a Better Society (SEBS)
clubs.description: Scientists and Engineers for a Better Society is a Columbia University student organization dedicated to creating increased awareness in the University community about scientific and technological issues of social relevance.

clubs.name: Student Advocates for the Arts
clubs.description: Student Advocates for the Arts (SAA) is a student-run club for learning about and participating in arts advocacy. Founded in 2002 by graduate students in the Arts Administration Program at Teachers College, Columbia University, SAA engages students in hands-on lobbying, workshops on advocacy and cultural policy, and discussions on the American system for funding the arts.

clubs.name: Students for Sanctuary
clubs.description: Students for Sanctuary strives to mobilize Columbia students to take action in the fight for immigration justice and reform.

clubs.name: Students Supporting Israel (SSI Columbia University)
clubs.description: Students Supporting Israel at Columbia University provides a space for all students to support, celebrate and advocate for Israel as part of an indigenous rights movement. The group empowers students to express their opinions regardless of political views.

clubs.name: Take Back the Night
clubs.description: The Columbia University Take Back the Night march and rally is an opportunity to speak out against all forms of sexual violence in our community.

clubs.name: ThinkIsrael
clubs.description: ThinkIsrael is a non-partisan discussion group that covers any and all topics relating to Israel by fostering interest in, excitement for, and debate about Israel, thinking both historically and contemporarily, open to people from all political, religious, ethnic, and ideological backgrounds.

clubs.name: American Academy of Environmental Engineers and Scientists of Columbia University
American Institute of Chemical Engineers
clubs.description: Columbia University's student chapter of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers provides prospective chemical engineers with information on the professional world and academic fields of study. It organizes events regarding networking, research, study breaks, plant tours and career fairs.

clubs.name: American Medical Students Association
clubs.description: Columbia University's student branch of American Medical Students Association, the largest independent national organization of medical students, offers opportunities to discover the many career paths available to physicians-in-training, while also learning about important health care issues at the local, regional and national levels.

clubs.name: American Society of Civil Engineers
clubs.description: Columbia University's student branch of American Society of Civil Engineers is a pre-professional student organization that aims to promote the personal and professional development of Civil Engineering students at Columbia University. It fosters interaction among students, faculty and industry professionals by organizing student projects and hosting several events throughout the year.

clubs.name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers
clubs.description: Columbia University's student chapter of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers hosts various events throughout the school year including career panels, graduate school panels, research seminars, social events and engineering talks.

clubs.name: Architecture Society
clubs.description: Architecture Society is a student-run group providing architectural awareness to undergraduate students at Columbia University and Barnard College. It gives a forum for students interested in architecture as a field of study to ask questions while also learning about graduate schools and the profession within the context of New York City.

clubs.name: Art Collective
clubs.description: ArtC is a student organization founded by students in the School of General Studies for creative minds with two major goals: to foster an artistic community where collaboration and exchange across all disciplines is encouraged, and to value the integration of business and art by launching professional development events.

clubs.name: Charles Drew Pre-Medical Society
clubs.description: The Charles Drew Pre-Medical Society is an organization that strives to guide, support and encourage premedical students, with a special emphasis on underrepresented minorities, in their various endeavors to become members of the medical field.

clubs.name: Columbia Alpha Partners
clubs.description: Columbia Alpha Partners is the engineering club that represents the Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research with hope to build a strong community through friendship, mentorship, and leadership.

clubs.name: Columbia Art Market Society
clubs.description:
The Columbia Art Market Society aims to encourage an interest in the intersection of art and business and educate our members on the happenings within the industry. CAMS wants to make art business accessible to all Columbia students and create a space on campus where they can learn more and engage with the

complexities of the art world.

clubs.name: Columbia Association for Women in Mathematics
clubs.description: The Association for Women in Mathematics Columbia Chapter is a pre-professional society whose mission is to encourage women and girls to study and have active careers in the mathematical sciences and to promote equal opportunities for women and girls in the field.

clubs.name: Columbia China Forum Group
clubs.description: ColumbiaChinaForum (CCF) is Columbia’s first undergraduate-led, China-focused Forum. A platform for constructive dialogue between the United States and China, CCF brings together leading figures in politics, academia, business, and beyond on China-related topics to share their insights and develop personal relationships with brilliant young individuals, to encourage diverse opinions and generate constructive advice on issues of mutual importance, and to chart a path for a prosperous and collaborative future.

clubs.name: Columbia Corporate Law and Business Association
clubs.description: The Columbia Corporate Law and Business Association is a pre-professional organization that promotes greater knowledge of world economies, with an emphasis on the impact of China. The group aims to prepare its members for careers in business, finance and law.

clubs.name: Columbia Financial Investment Group (CFIG)
clubs.description: The Columbia Financial Investment Group is Columbia University’s largest undergraduate finance club in New York City. It aims to encourage an interest in finance and inform all members of the financial markets.

clubs.name: Columbia Global Research and Consulting Group
clubs.description: The goal of Columbia Global Research and Consulting Group is to provide services in management consulting, policy research, data analytics, and finance to leave a lasting impact on the local and international community. By supporting nonprofit organizations and public sector agencies, Columbia Global Research and Consulting Group aims to advance social impact projects in all stages of development and execution. Through this service, Columbia Global Research and Consulting Group seeks to provide opportunities for career advancement, skill development, education, and activism for its members.

clubs.name: Columbia Marketing Club
clubs.description: Columbia Marketing Club (CMC) is Columbia’s premier undergraduate organization dedicated to all things related to marketing and brand.

clubs.name: Columbia Organization of Rising Entrepreneurs (CORE)
clubs.description: Columbia Entrepreneurship, Innovation, and Design (also known as Columbia Entrepreneurship) was founded in the summer of 2013 at the direction of University President Lee C. Bollinger and the University Board of Trustees to support, invigorate, accelerate and motivate Columbia University community programs and culture around innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship.

clubs.name: Columbia Quant Group
clubs.description: Columbia Quant Group (CQG) is Columbia University's premier Quantitative Finance organization on campus and is open to all undergraduate and graduate students. Our goal is to educate and connect quantitatively-oriented students with professionals in the quantitative finance industry.

clubs.name: Columbia Undergraduate Consulting Club
clubs.description: The Columbia Undergraduate Consulting Club seeks to educate students about the world of consulting while preparing them to enter the industry. Through informational events, case study workshops, networking opportunities and active projects in consulting, the group offers students unparallelled opportunities to learn and advance as problem solvers and team players.

clubs.name: Columbia University Black Pre-Professional Society
clubs.description: The mission of the Columbia University Black Pre-Professional Society is to provide Black Columbia students with the hard and soft skills they need to successfully navigate the professional careers of their choosing. CUBPS aims to create an environment that not only educates its members, but also provides them with the support and guidance necessary to formulate and actualize career goals.

clubs.name: Columbia University EMS
clubs.description: CUEMS, formerly Columbia Area Volunteer Ambulance, is a student-operated, New York State certified, Basic Life Support (BLS) volunteer ambulance corps that provides prehospital emergency medical care, free of charge, to Columbia University's Morningside Heights Campus and surrounding area 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. The corps has approximately 45 active members and responds to over 1100 emergency calls per year.

clubs.name: Columbia University Fashion Society (CUFS)
clubs.description: Columbia University Fashion Society (CUFS) aims to develop well-informed future leaders in the fashion industry through pre-professionally focused panels, discussions, networking sessions, and more.

clubs.name: Columbia University Women in Law and Politics
clubs.description: Columbia University Women in Law and Politics is an organization founded to create a community of support and progress. It aims to combine the educational goals of a pre-professional organization with the ongoing and necessary conversations about gender parity in both law and politics.

clubs.name: Columbia Venture Partners
clubs.description: Columbia Venture Partners is Columbia’s leading venture capital initiative for the undergraduate student body, with a focus on bringing opportunities from the broader VC community to campus.

clubs.name: CUINFORMS
clubs.description: CU Informs is made up of undergraduate and graduate students whose purpose is to promote interest in the fields of operations research and the management sciences. The group facilitates the exchange of ideas, a sense of community and mentorship within these fields.

clubs.name: Economics Society
clubs.description: Columbia Economics Society is the largest pre-professional group on campus serving undergraduates at the University. It organizes events to connect students with economists, professors and professionals from banking, finance and consulting fields.

clubs.name: Engineers Without Borders
clubs.description: Engineers Without Borders USA supports community-driven development programs worldwide by collaborating with local partners to design and implement sustainable engineering projects, while creating transformative experiences and responsible leaders. Founded in 2004, Columbia University's student chapter follows this mission by working on sustainable engineering projects in Ghana, Morocco and Uganda.

clubs.name: Global China Connection
clubs.description: Global China Connection is an organization for University students and young professionals of all nationalities looking to engage with China’s emergence in the world. It connects future leaders from all nations and assists them in developing the skills and friendships necessary to succeed both in China and internationally.

clubs.name: Institute of Electronics and Electrical Engineers
clubs.description: The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers at Columbia University is a pre-professional society that promotes professional development among electrical engineering and computer engineering students.

clubs.name: Korean International Society for Academics and Career (KISAC)
clubs.description: Korean International Society for Academics and Career is a pre-professional club, which focuses on professional development for Korean international students.

clubs.name: Koreans in General Studies
clubs.description: KIGS encourages Korean students and alumni to share their professional experiences and enrich the communities at Columbia University and in New York City.

clubs.name: Multicultural Business Association
clubs.description: The Multicultural Business Association is an undergraduate pre-professional organization that strives to bridge the gap between Columbia’s student body and large businesses by providing students with the opportunities and resources necessary to achieve their professional career goals.

clubs.name: National Society of Black Engineers
clubs.description: At Columbia University, the National Society of Black Engineers chapter has established itself both as a premier pre-professional organization on campus and as an exceptional chapter in the region. Its focal points include: quality over quantity, effective communication, engaging membership and training future leaders.

clubs.name: Pre-Law Society
clubs.description: Columbia University Undergraduate Law Society seeks to provide a forum where undergraduate students can learn about the law school application and admissions process, law schools and the legal profession in general through interaction with practicing attorneys, educators and law students.

clubs.name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
clubs.description: The members of the Columbia Chapter of The Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers aim to serve as role models in the Hispanic community.

clubs.name: Society of Women Engineers
clubs.description: The Columbia Society of Women Engineers' mission is to encourage women to achieve their full potential in careers as engineers and leaders. The group also aims to demonstrate the value of diversity and to expand the image of the engineering profession as a positive force.

clubs.name: TAMID at Columbia
clubs.description: TAMID Group at Columbia develops the professional skills of undergraduate students through hands-on interaction with the Israeli economy. Our members take part in a comprehensive education curriculum, pro-bono consulting for Israeli startups, capital market investment research, and a summer internship program in Israel.

clubs.name: The Women's Network: Columbia
clubs.description: The Women’s Network cultivates and celebrates women's ambition through connecting our members to industry leaders, professional development resources, and career opportunities. The Women’s Network: Columbia is one chapter of the broader nationwide organization.

clubs.name: Womens Business Society
clubs.description: The Columbia Women's Business Society is an undergraduate women's organization that aims to create a business leadership network among University students and female professionals in New York City and beyond.

clubs.name: Atheist and Agnostic Students Society
clubs.description: The Atheist and Agnostic Students Society (AASS), currently in formation, wishes to serve as a voice for non-theist students at Columbia University. AASS aspires to be a social and intellectual community for nonbelievers at Columbia University.

clubs.name: Baha'i Club
clubs.description: The Baha'i Club is a student group whose membership is not confined to members of the Baha'i Faith. Its main purposes are to bring people together in a spirit of friendship, to promote independent and unprejudiced thinking, to foster unity among different racial, ethnic and religious groups on campus, and to collaborate with like-minded organizations.

clubs.name: Canterbury Club (Episcopalian Society)
clubs.description: The Columbia Canterbury Club is a student organization at the University that seeks to support students by creating a campus community for pursuing spirituality in the modern world, offering Sunday services and providing connection to the Episcopal Church in New York.

clubs.name: Chabad Student Network
clubs.description: Chabad is a Jewish organization that places families internationally to help foster a warm environment for communal and religious life. Chabad at Columbia University is a meeting place for social, educational and cultural events, where students can seek guidance on whatever issues life presents.

clubs.name: Christian Union Lumine
clubs.description: Christian Union Lumine is a Christian leadership ministry that serves all four undergraduate colleges of Columbia University. Supported by Christian Union, the group aims to give Columbia University students who identify as Christians the tools to live faith-filled lives, spread the Gospel and commune in Christ.

clubs.name: Columbia Catholic Ministry
clubs.description: Columbia Catholic Ministry, formerly known as Columbia Catholic Undergraduates, includes students from Columbia College, Columbia Engineering, Barnard College and the School of General Studies who form a close-knit fellowship that strives to integrate the Catholic faith into their daily lives.

clubs.name: Columbia SOON Movement
clubs.description: Columbia SOON Movement is an inter-denominational ministry that holds weekly worship services, prayer meetings, Bible studies, study breaks and other activities.

clubs.name: Columbia University Latter-Day Saint Student Association
clubs.description: The Columbia University Latter-day Saint Student Association (LDSSA) brings together Mormon and Mormon-adjacent students for discussion of the ways that LDS religious identity intersects with society and academia.

clubs.name: Compass Christian Koinonia (CCK)
clubs.description: CCK, a Christian fellowship group at Columbia University, is a community of CC, SEAS, Barnard and graduate students with a common desire to learn more about Jesus and share our faith with others.

clubs.name: CU Sewa
clubs.description: Columbia University Sewa is a social justice and community service organization that is based upon the Sikh value of sewa (selfless service). Sewa hosts events that challenge and address injustices and social issues affecting marginalized communities.

clubs.name: Falun Dafa Club at Columbia University
clubs.description: Falun Dafa Club at Columbia University aims to promote ancient ways to improve mind and body. The group also studies spiritual teachings, with core principles of truthfulness, compassion and forbearance.

clubs.name: Intervarsity Christian Fellowship (IVCF)
clubs.description: InterVarsity Christian Fellowship is an inter-denominational Christian fellowship at Columbia University, with the aim to promote God's word.

clubs.name: Kesher
clubs.description: Kesher is a community for Reform Jewish students on the Columbia University campus that hosts weekly Shabbat services (followed by free vegetarian dinner), as well as social and educational programming.

clubs.name: Koach
clubs.description: Koach is the Traditional-Egalitarian community that serves Conservative Jewish students of Columbia, Barnard, and JTS. All are welcome to join us for weekly Shabbat Services (and Saturday morning lunch!), social gatherings both in and out of Hillel, and our varied educational opportunities. Koach is an exciting, innovative community that is committed to reaching all students regardless of experience.

clubs.name: Lalekhet
clubs.description: Lalekhet, Columbia/Barnard Hillel’s partnership minyan, hosts lectures, potluck meals, and (most importantly) spirited prayer services on Friday nights and Saturday afternoons that encourage participation from both men and women, based on the conviction that tradition and modernity belong in conversation with each other–a conversation through which each can inform and enrich the other.

clubs.name: Lishma: Jewish Learning
clubs.description: The Beit Midrash Committee creates Jewish learning experiences that enable students to think broadly and deeply about Judaism and Jewish texts. This learning takes many forms, and we organize both traditional and unconventional opportunities to broaden and strength our Jewish identities and commitments.

clubs.name: Muslim Students Association (MSA)
clubs.description: Muslim Students Association aims to foster Muslim life on campus and strengthen the bonds among its allies, associates and members within the Columbia University community.

clubs.name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship (OCF)
clubs.description: Orthodox Christian Fellowship is the official collegiate campus ministry program under the Assembly of Canonical Orthodox Bishops of the United States of America. The group strives to connect Orthodox college students—and those interested in the Orthodox Christian faith—to Christ and His Church.

clubs.name: Reformed University Fellowship
clubs.description: Reformed University Fellowship is a community at Columbia University where Christians can grow in their faith and where those who are skeptical or curious can bring their questions.

clubs.name: Save the Earth from A to Z (ASEZ)
clubs.description: Save the Earth from A to Z (ASEZ) is a volunteer club that originates from college youth members of the World Mission Society Church of God. Seeking to impact the world through the love of Mother, the group aims to implement the UN SDGs through effective volunteer efforts on campus and in the community. Our activities promote a sense of civic responsibility, equipping the youth with the skills and expertise necessary to solve the escalating global challenges.

clubs.name: Shabbat Meals Committee
clubs.description: Shabbat Meals Committee (SMC) works to make weekly Shabbat dinners at Hewitt dining hall a fun, welcoming, and social experience every week.

clubs.name: The Columbia Witness
clubs.description: The Columbia Witness, formerly known as Columbia Crown and Cross, exists to share Christian perspectives in our academic and largely secular environment. Through our print issues, blog and public events, it aims to engage our community with thoughtful discussions about our diverse worldviews.

clubs.name: Veritas Forum
clubs.description: The Veritas Forum at Columbia University hosts conversations where students can engage in discussions dealing with some of life’s weightiest topics: morality, purpose and faith.

clubs.name: Wednesday Night Learning Program
clubs.description: Wednesday Night Learning Program (WNLP) is a weekly program that serves as a space for students to learn Jewish texts in an informal, unstructured setting in pairs, in groups, or on their own, regardless of background, comfort level, or ability.

clubs.name: Yavneh
clubs.description: Yavneh, the Orthodox student community on campus, aims to provide a home for students on campus looking for a welcoming and committed Orthodox community by infusing Modern Orthodox values into our social, educational, chessed, and religious programming.

clubs.name: The Food Pantry at Columbia
clubs.description: The Food Pantry at Columbia provides non-perishable food for students with any level of food insecurity. Its mission is to relieve hunger through the acquisition and distribution of food to those students who most need it and to lead our campus community in the fight against hunger.

clubs.name: Advocacy Coalition
clubs.description: Advocacy Coalition volunteers work with homeless and low-income clients at TASC and ESOL classes and other community venues. Volunteers act as advocates by providing clients with referrals to shelters, pantries, treatment facilities, and job training programs and by helping clients to become aware of government benefit systems.

clubs.name: African Development Group
clubs.description: The African Development Group - Columbia University was established with a mission to reverse brain drain by promoting a deeper engagement with the African Diaspora in African development through research, initiative and service.

clubs.name: AfterHours Tutoring
clubs.description: After-Hours Tutoring provides one-on-one homework help and tutoring to elementary and middle school students in reading and math, as well as subjects such as science and social studies. The program operates in partnership with the Volunteers of America Regent Family Residence, a transitional shelter serving 140 families. Tutoring occurs at the Regent from 3:30pm - 5:30pm Mondays through Thursdays and serves students generally ranging from grades 3 to 9.

clubs.name: Alice! Health Promotion Peer Leaders
clubs.description: CU Well Peer Leaders facilitate honest conversations with students about alcohol and other drug issues and healthy lifestyle behaviors. This leadership position offers an opportunity to learn about alcohol and other drug issues, stress management, and healthy lifestyle behaviors. Peer leaders speak to incoming first-years about managing choices as they transition into the Columbia community; and they act as campus leaders throughout the year on outreach initiatives to create a smart, safe, responsible, and well University community.

clubs.name: Alternative Break Program
clubs.description: The Alternative Break Program (ABP) funds and supports students who aim to address community challenges around the world, across the country or in our own backyards! This program differs from more traditional community service or spring break service trips: the ABP invites students themselves — with help from faculty, administrators and fellow students — to develop their own civic engagement projects, rather than a more traditional model where an administrator organizes the program and students participate.

clubs.name: America Reads
clubs.description: America Reads at Community Impact is one of 1,200 chapters at colleges and universities nationwide. We endeavor to improve literacy at three public schools, P.S. 125, P.S. 192 and P.S. 76, in the Morningside Heights and West Harlem communities. We provide daytime in-class assistance and after school one-on-one tutoring for students in grades K-5. Tutors also seek to nurture the value and joy of learning through mentorship and organize weekly educational field trips around the city. Volunteers can choose to work one session per week (2 hours with travel) or several sessions per week for one year.

clubs.name: Artists Reaching Out
clubs.description: Artists Reaching Out (ARO) brings arts education to Pre-school-5th grade students who presently have limited opportunities for enrichment in the arts. Volunteers foster positive mentoring relationships and cultivate young talent in the areas of drama, music, fine art, creative writing, and dance. ARO volunteer teachers lead students both during the school day and in after school programs.

clubs.name: Asian Youth Program
clubs.description: Asian Youth Program (AYP), in partnership with New York Asian Women’s Center, offers mentoring to children impacted by domestic violence. AYP mentors become positive role models engaging in one-to-one relationships through enrichment activities and recreational trips to cultural sites around New York City. All activities are designed to build self-confidence, foster a sense of family and community, and inspire a commitment to service among the children served in a fun and nurturing environment.

clubs.name: Barnard/Columbia Design For America (DFA)
clubs.description: Barnard/Columbia Design for America is part of a national network of passionate young thinkers and activists revolutionizing the way college students engage with and improve the world. The group aims to use its energy and resources to design and implement local, sustainable projects with the potential for national impact.

clubs.name: Best Buddies
clubs.description: Best Buddies promotes the social inclusion and acceptance of individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities (IDD) by matching CU students with community members who have IDD. Together, our members with and without disabilities launch advocacy efforts, volunteer nearby, and attend bonding events such as picnics, museum outings, baking events, and sports games. Volunteer commitment of 1 or 2 outings per month and 1 chapter meeting each month.

clubs.name: Big SIBS
clubs.description: Big SIBS is one of Community Impact’s founding programs. It provides a unique mentoring opportunity for local youth, called Littles, who would benefit from a positive adult role model. Littles, from the communities of Harlem, Washington Heights, and Morningside Heights, are paired with BIGS from Columbia or Barnard who build a big brother/sister relationship. Growing together, sharing experiences, and developing trust and friendship provides Littles with stable, ongoing companionship. Big SIBS requires a minimum two-year commitment with weekly outings lasting 3-5 hours. Sessions are every Sunday from 10:00am - 2:00pm.

clubs.name: Blue Key Society
clubs.description: The Blue Key Society is Columbia University's oldest community service organization. The organization serves the University by linking Columbia University's academic and social communities with local and national charitable organizations through fundraisers, campus-wide events and philanthropic pursuits.

clubs.name: Brain Exercise Initiative Columbia
clubs.description: Brain Exercise Initiative uses simple math, writing, and reading-aloud exercises as an intervention to improve cognitive function in those with Alzheimer's Disease or other neurodegenerative disorders at partnered residential homes. We encourage awareness of these disorders and work to establish an invaluable, all-too-rare avenue for intergenerational service, discussion, and collaboration.

clubs.name: Camp Kesem
clubs.description: Camp Kesem is a nationwide community driven by passionate college student leaders that supports children, whose parents are affected by cancer, with free summer camps. The experience provides a peer-support network and strengthens communications skills for the children.

clubs.name: Challah for Hunger
clubs.description: Challah for Hunger is a national student organization that raises money and awareness for hunger-relief through the production and sale of challah. The club meets to bake challah bi-weekly, and holds several educational activities a semester.

clubs.name: CityStep Columbia
clubs.description: CityStep Columbia is the first dance and creative expression group to increase both student and community youth involvement, self-awareness, and confidence by leading movement-based activity for local children in NYC public schools. Inspired by the principles found online at citystep.org, we explore relevant themes such as life in the city, historic and current events, art, and literature as students and children alike transmit their own creative mindset and shared passion for movement throughout the community.

clubs.name: College Road
clubs.description: College Road is not a class, but a complete package of services designed to help you through every step of the college application process. Counselors work with students one-on-one to find the right college for them, complete admissions applications, and explore financial aid and funding options. College tours and campus visits are also arranged so that students can be confident with the schools they have selected. At the end of this process we will even help pay for testing and application fees.

clubs.name: Columbia University Red Cross
clubs.description: The purpose of American Red Cross at Columbia University to is provide relief to victims of disasters and help people prevent, prepare for, and respond to emergencies both locally and abroad.

clubs.name: Columbia University Science Olympiad
clubs.description: Columbia University Science Olympiad is an undergraduate-led organization dedicated to improving and expanding the experience of middle and high school students in Science Olympiad. Our activities include volunteering at Science Olympiad tournaments in the NYC area and nationwide and organizing an annual invitational tournament.

clubs.name: Columbia Youth Adventurers
clubs.description: Columbia Youth Adventurers (CYA) is a social excursion and mentorship program that provides low-income children an opportunity to engage in learning and enrichment activities outside of the classroom. Barnard and Columbia volunteers lead cultural and recreational trips to sites around the city. The program seeks to foster self-esteem, an appreciation of cultural activities and traditions, and a passion for education and learning. Weekly sessions are from 10am-2pm Saturday at various locations.

clubs.name: Columbia-Bronx Oncology Living Daily Program
clubs.description: Columbia BOLD arose to bolster the medical system of one of the poorest districts in the U.S.: Bronx, New York. Representing volunteers from across the city, we represent the desire for university students and other volunteers everywhere to diminish the stark inequalities facing cancer patients today.

clubs.name: Community Impact
clubs.description: Community Impact seeks to advance the public good by engaging Columbia University students in high-quality service in partnership with community organizations that meet critical community needs, develop student leadership, connect service and learning, and foster an environment of mutual respect in the neighborhoods surrounding the university.

clubs.name: Community Lunch
clubs.description: Community Lunch volunteers work as a team every Friday to cook a meal from scratch for 75-100 homeless and low-income guests. Our Community Lunch program, located at the Broadway Presbyterian Church on 114th Street and Broadway, is unique for its family-style serving and inviting environment. Volunteers organize holiday parties for homeless and low-income children and fundraising events to support program goals and food justice issues.

clubs.name: Consult Your Community - Columbia University
clubs.description: Consult Your Communicty - Columbia University provides pro bono management and strategy consulting services for local small businesses. Its mission is to aid local businesses in the face of gentrification and increased corporate competitiveness.

clubs.name: Gay Health Advocacy Project
clubs.description: Gay Health Advocacy Project advocates are student volunteers trained to address a broad range of issues pertaining to sexual and emotional health. Advocates provide information about the prevention and treatment of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections (STIs), as well as the psychological factors connected to these issues.

clubs.name: Girls Who Code
clubs.description: Columbia Girls Who Code is a chapter of the national organization of Girls Who Code. The group teaches women in the local community the basics of coding to encourage participation in the field from more women.

clubs.name: Habitat for Humanity
clubs.description: According to a study conducted by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, an estimated 600,000 persons in the United States are without a home. New York City is by no means immune to the crisis, with over 55,000 of its own inhabitants currently utilizing the NYC shelter systems. Lack of secure housing stands as a major cause of various other social problems such as the deterioration of mental health and drug addiction. Aiming to curb this growing trend of homelessness and all its tangential problems, Habitat for Humanity tackles this issue directly by constructing safe, affordable homes. The Columbia University Chapter, in collaboration with Habitat NYC, continues to contribute to the greater effort to provide houses for those who need them most.

clubs.name: Health Education Awareness League (HEAL)
clubs.description: Health Education and Awareness League (HEAL) volunteers teach health awareness to middle-school children attending public schools in Harlem. Volunteers also meet weekly to create a dynamic and interactive curriculum, covering preventative health, nutrition, drugs, careers in health professions and other relevant topics.

clubs.name: Health LEADS
clubs.description: Health Leads volunteers work at family help desks at Harlem Hospital. They work directly with patients, doctors, and nurses to link patients with eligible health insurance and other programs such as food pantries, adult education and employment as requested. Volunteers also follow-up with patients and doctors and attend reflection session to discuss issues in public health and poverty and to talk about program development. The advocate commitment is approximately 5 hours per week, on and off campus.

clubs.name: Hearts for the Homeless International at Columbia
clubs.description: Our group represents the NYC branch of the greater organization Hearts for the Homeless international. On a weekly basis we go to the Harlem Salvation Army and person blood pressure checks and offer heart advice under the guidance of the founder of H4H who is also in his residency at Columbia. Additionally we organize the shipment of necessary supplies to the Ukraine branch of our organization.

clubs.name: Heights to Heights Mentoring
clubs.description: Heights to Heights (H2H) matches mentors from Columbia and Barnard College with middle school students who have recently immigrated to the U.S. H2H provides a supportive environment in which the students can improve their English conversational skills, form strong relationships with their mentors, develop important life skills, and gain cultural enrichment through exposure to education and cultural activities. Sessions are held on campus on Fridays from 3pm - 5pm.

clubs.name: Job Road
clubs.description: Job Road counselors work alongside students to develop their career goals through job readiness workshops and one-on-one counseling appointments. Our counselors teach students how to create and tailor their resumes and cover letters to specific job opportunities, conduct themselves in interviews, and search the internet for job opportunities. Job Road counselors at Community Impact are committed to not only assisting you with the practical aspects of career development, but are invested in your long-term success.

clubs.name: Jobs and Education Empowerment Project - TASC, ESOL and CAT Prep
clubs.description: Our education classes for adults are overseen by C.I.'s Jobs and Education Empowerment Project (J.E.E.P) program which helps adult residents of the neighborhood further their education and find jobs. Programs operate on the Columbia University and Barnard College campuses. We offer TASC, Spanish TASC, ESOL and CUNY Assessment Test (CAT) Prep support. Once you register for TASC you will be asked to sit a placement test to determine your readiness to sit the TASC test. In addition there is support for job and college applications. Likewise, particpants intending to take ESOL classes will be assessed as to their level of English proficiency.

clubs.name: Let's Get Ready
clubs.description: Let’s Get Ready! at Columbia is part of a network of 30 such programs at colleges and universities in Eastern states. Volunteers work with students at Frederick Douglass Academy in Harlem to raise SAT scores, complete college applications, and acquaint students to college life. The program offers free SAT preparation courses and college and financial aid advising to underserved high school students and their families. Volunteers can choose to serve from 6pm - 8pm on Monday or Thursday evening.

clubs.name: Mentoring Youth in NYC
clubs.description: Mentoring Youth in NYC (MyNYC) is a mentoring program that works with high school students who will become first generation college students, providing them mentors and resources for the college application process, assistance that would otherwise be unavailable. Mentors advise high school students on building strong college applications and share information on what to expect in the college experience, including choosing a major, managing time, and respecting diversity. Additionally, MyNYC's off campus, one-on-one outings are designed to foster trusting relationships between the mentors and their mentees. Sessions run from 4:00pm - 5:30pm on Fridays in Earl Hall at Columbia. Volunteer commitment is for one year.

clubs.name: Model Congress
clubs.description: Columbia University Model Congress is a simulation of government for high school students that is hosted at Columbia University.

clubs.name: New York Small Claims Advisory Service at Columbia (NYSCAS)
clubs.description: The New York Small Claims Advisory Service (NYSCAS) aims to assist socioeconomically disadvantaged New York City residents in navigating the small claims court system. NYSCAS volunteers work directly with clients on matters including labor, housing, and consumer disputes, providing clients with information regarding New York City specific law, small claims procedure, and effective court presentations.

clubs.name: One-to-One Tutoring
clubs.description: One-to-One Tutoring provides individual tutoring to elementary school children for hour-and-a-half sessions on Saturdays, on Columbia's Morningside campus. Tutoring is open to any students aged 6-12 who live or attend school in the neighborhoods of Morningside Heights, Washington Heights, and Harlem. Tutors help students to improve Math and reading skills, and encourage students to develop effective studying habits. Tutors also aim to provide their tutees with the tools required to persevere in their studies, and the ability to face challenging concepts with confidence. Volunteer commitment is for an hour and a half every Saturday morning, between 10am and 2pm, for one year.

clubs.name: Peace by PEACE
clubs.description: Peace by PEACE is a conflict resolution skill development program for elementary school students. Volunteer teachers offer a year-long curriculum, fostering ways of resolving differences by communicating, understanding different points of view, and learning together. Weekly one-hour sessions take place on Friday afternoons at partner schools and a family shelter.

clubs.name: Project for the Homeless
clubs.description: Project for the Homeless (PFH) is a student organization that staffs two small homeless shelters in the Upper West Side of Manhattan, the men's shelter at Stephen Wise Free Synagogue and the women's shelter at the New York Society for Ethical Culture. By having Columbia and Barnard students as nightly supervisors, PFH ensures that the two shelters remain open for 120 nights for the men and women who are in need of a place to stay in the City of New York.

clubs.name: Project Tutors
clubs.description: Project Tutors pairs volunteers in classrooms to assist students and support teachers. Volunteers support classroom teachers by offering students individual attention, serving as one-to-one and small group tutors, and providing extra support in the classroom in an assistant teacher role. Tutors are assigned to a specific teacher and are expected to tutor at least one session per week (2 hours with travel).

clubs.name: Robogals
clubs.description: Robogals is a student-run organization that aims to increase female participation in engineering and and technology through fun and educational initiatives aimed at girls in primary and secondary school.

clubs.name: Sci-Inspire
clubs.description: The Sci-Inspire Chapter at Columbia University seeks to connect undergraduate STEM students with a network of local schools in Harlem. Through volunteer work, the organization strives to improve the participation of underprivileged and underrepresented minorities in the STEM fields.

clubs.name: Sexual Violence Response Peer Advocates and Peer Educators
clubs.description:
Peer advocates provide survivors and their supporters with confidential emotional support, accompaniment, and referrals to on- and off-campus resources. They also help survivors make informed decisions about their medical, legal, and disciplinary options. Peer advocates receive 40 hours of training and are supervised by advisers at Columbia and Barnard.

Peer educators with the Sexual Violence Response program are students of all gender identities committed to preventing sexual and intimate partner violence and to educating their peers about healthy relationships and sexuality.

clubs.name: Sharsheret
clubs.description: The purpose of Sharsheret at Columbia/Barnard Hillel is to raise awareness about breast and ovarian cancer and their prevalence within the Jewish community on campus. We hope to encourage students to learn about their medical history and ask their doctors questions and, if necessary, empower them to take preventive measures.

clubs.name: Stressbusters
clubs.description: Stressbusters are student volunteers who help others learn strategies for coping with stress. They also provide free brief neck and back rubs and facilitate arts and crafts activities throughout the Morningside Columbia community.

clubs.name: STRIVE
clubs.description: STRIVE provides intensive one on one academic tutoring, mentoring, peer support, and disease management education to low-income minority teenagers in New York City living with sickle cell disease.

clubs.name: Student Health Outreach Program
clubs.description: Student Health Outreach Program (SHOUT) volunteers educate families about the availability of health insurance and other government benefits and provide eligibility and screenings. Volunteers serve in community-based organizations, St Mary's Church on W126th St, BCI on Broadway and 114th St. SHOUT partners with two active non-profits, SeedCo and Children’s Defense Fund for training and enrollment activities. Volunteer commitment of 3 hours/week, various days, off-campus.

clubs.name: Students for Health Education, Access, and Literacy (S-HEAL)
clubs.description: S-HEAL works with high schools that lack health education and in which the majority of the students live at or below the poverty line. These students experience a disproportionate number of serious health risks ranging from teenage pregnancy to obesity.

clubs.name: Terence Cardinal Cooke At Your Service Volunteer Program
clubs.description: The “At Your Service” Volunteer Program is a student-run volunteer program at Terence Cardinal Cooke Health Care Center, a sub-acute rehab center and skilled nursing facility.

clubs.name: Toddler Learning Center
clubs.description: Toddler Learning Center (TLC) is an early childhood education program for toddlers from Harlem and Morningside Heights. Volunteers engage toddlers in interactive and educational activities via an anti-bias, play-based curriculum geared to help toddlers enjoy learning. TLC volunteers provide program activities on Saturdays from 10:00am - 2:00pm.

clubs.name: UNICEF
clubs.description: Columbia UNICEF is part of a national coalition of student-led campus groups that educate, advocate and fundraise on behalf of UNICEF. It believes that every child has the right the survive and thrive in this world.

clubs.name: Youth For Debate
clubs.description: Youth for Debate, Inc. was founded at Columbia University in 2009 with the purpose of improving education in public schools through debate and public speaking instruction. The service organization encourages students to think critically and advocate for themselves.

clubs.name: Active Minds
clubs.description: Columbia University's chapter of Active Minds, a nationwide non-profit organization that works to increase students’ awareness of mental health issues, provides information and resources, encourages students to seek help and serves as liaison between students and the mental health community.

clubs.name: Anime Club
clubs.description: Anime Club provides opportunity for students to watch and discuss anime shows and play games with the purpose of promoting shared cultural and technological interests through animation.

clubs.name: Artist Society
clubs.description: Artist Society aims to answer the call of many University affiliates who want focused studio time but could not fit visual arts classes into their schedules. The group provides an environment where all visual artists at Columbia University can meet, relax and create.

clubs.name: Bacchanal
clubs.description: Bacchanal is committed to upholding traditions of Columbia University’s premier annual concert Bacchanal, a show featuring professional artists and student musical acts. The group strives to foster a sense of community through music while putting on a fun and safe show for its peers.

clubs.name: Chess Club
clubs.description: Columbia University Chess Club is open to anyone interested in playing and/or learning about chess. It holds weekly meeting and other activities, such as lectures and competitions.

clubs.name: Columbia Bartending Agency
clubs.description: The Columbia School of Mixology has been training bartenders since 1965 and in that time our graduates have gone on to find great success in every level of the business. From bars to clubs to private staffing and catering, you can be sure that a Columbia School of Mixology graduate has worked there. All our classes are taught right on Columbia University's Morningside Heights campus.

clubs.name: Columbia Minecraft Club (CMC)
clubs.description: The purpose of the Columbia Minecraft Club is to foster a community for Columbia University students who play Minecraft. Although we started off playing the game together casually, this eventually evolved into us meeting regularly, in person, beginning in the Fall of 2019. The Columbia Minecraft Club was founded in the Summer of 2019. Since its creation, we have hosted weekly general body meetings alongside other special events. Server launches, Minecon Live, skin design contests, building competitions, Bedwars Game Nights, and yearly anniversary celebrations. The Columbia Minecraft Club is dedicated to building community, reducing stress, and being welcoming to all.

clubs.name: Columbia Poker Club
clubs.description: Columbia Poker Club is a community for people to learn, discuss, and enjoy the game of poker. We welcome players of any background and teach all levels of poker strategy, from the rules and fundamentals to advanced poker theory.

clubs.name: Columbia Recovery Coalition
clubs.description: The Columbia Recovery Coalition is an association of Columbia University students dedicated to the unique concerns and interests of those who are in recovery, or may be interested in recovery, from any substance abuse or other emotional or traumatic situation.

clubs.name: Columbia University Culinary Society
clubs.description: The Columbia University Culinary Society is the perfect place for food enthusiasts on campus! Join to help plan all cooking related events, ranging from bake-offs to potlucks to Columbia University Restaurant Week.

clubs.name: Columbia University Family Student Network (CUFSN)
clubs.description: Columbia University Family Support Network is a University-wide organization focused on advocating for improved resources and policies to support members of the Columbia University community with families.

clubs.name: Columbia University Formula Racing
clubs.description: Columbia University Formula Racing is Columbia University's race car team, a group of highly motivated students who design, build and drive a high-performance race car. Undergraduates and graduates of all majors are welcome to join this cohesive community.

clubs.name: Columbia University Gaming Group
clubs.description: Founded in 2014 as Columbia Esports, this club was started by a group of friends who just loved to play video games. Around the same time, the Game Design and Development Club was founded with the goal of uniting students who were interested in building and exploring game design. In 2025, the two clubs merged and incorporated the Rhythm Games club as well, creating Columbia University Gaming Group. CUGG has expanded its programming to encompass more than just competitive gaming, fostering an inclusive and supportive community for everyone involved in the gaming community.

clubs.name: Columbia University Gardening Club
clubs.description: Columbia University Gardening’s purpose is to produce and maintain a productive, healthy garden throughout the year, and to teach students about growing and eating their own food, as well as providing a community of people who respect the environment and care about saving it. Its final purpose is to host, cohost, and promote events that teach students about gardening, food, and the earth. Many of our gardeners have some family member or ancestor who has farmed before: we provide students with the unique opportunity of reconnecting with their roots and re-learning vital skills that produce food for life, directly on Columbia’s campus. We also hope to provide more gardening space for growing in the future and more volunteer opportunities, as we collect more gardeners, so that all members can play a significant role in developing their own care, taste, and skill for working the earth.

clubs.name: Columbia University Gourmand Club
clubs.description: Gourmand is a community empowering the next generation of food lovers and leaders! We are a food interest group open to all Columbia students that aims to connect the campus community to the broader food scene in NYC by hosting food-related events, including neighborhood food treks and supper clubs, and producing digital content through our social media and blog.

clubs.name: Columbia University Society for Baseball Research (SBR)
clubs.description: The purpose of this organization shall be to curate, create, and publish novel baseball research from the greater Columbia community and promote an accessible learning platform for Columbia students and faculty to grow baseball knowledge.

clubs.name: Columbia Vegan Society
clubs.description: The Columbia Vegan Society is an academic community that seeks to engage students and professionals on topics related to public health, sustainability and bioethics. The goal of the group is to legitimize veganism by focusing on professional conduct and effective outreach.

clubs.name: Engineering Recruitment Committee (ERC)
clubs.description: The ERC is a selective organization whose mission is to support engineering outreach initiatives within Columbia Undergraduate Admissions and provide a Columbia Engineering-focused student perspective to prospective students.

clubs.name: Games Club
clubs.description: Founded in 1977, Columbia University Games Club is an organization for students in the university to play all sorts of games including board games, war games, role-playing games, head games, games of chance, games of strategy and games of cunning.

clubs.name: Global Recruitment Committee (GRC)
